title: Changelog
description: Release notes for OpenBox, from the latest release back to the first build.
body: 3.0.0 (2026-11-19) — The Rust-y Box The largest release in the project. The entire Python backend is replaced by a standalone native Rust server, openbox-server (ADR 0115), spanning 15 workspace crates, 170 migrated backend modules, and 417 HTTP endpoints (413 public /api/v2/ routes plus 4 /api/host/ native-window routes). Every packaged build ships the Rust binary with zero bundled CPython . Formal scale graduates to 50,000 games (ADR 0116). Five new player features ship alongside a desktop UI and usability redesign. Library schema 7 is unchanged: a 2.0 or 2.1 library opens without migration. Added - Native Rust backend. openbox-server replaces the Python server in the AppImage, Flatpak, Windows portable zips, and the universal macOS bundle. Linux AppImages are 9.7 MiB (x86_64) and 9.0 MiB (aarch64); the Flatpak is 7.1 MiB; Windows zips are 14.6 MiB (x86_64) and 13.8 MiB (ARM64); the macOS bundle is 17.4 MiB (59.1% smaller). - 50,000-game scale. At 50,000 games the Rust server finishes the benchmark at 468.8 MB RSS, with cover serving 5,867x faster, Explorer facets 142.1x faster, and delta search 82.6x faster than the Python 3.0 build. library.json remains canonical and human-readable. - Save Vault (ADR 0109). Indexed, SHA-256-verified save snapshots triggered manually, on session close ( save_vault_on_close ), or on a schedule ( save_vault_auto_days ). Restores take a mandatory pre-restore safety snapshot, shared emulator roots are excluded, and the tabbed Save History dialog exposes snapshot, restore, diff, and delete. Vault data lives under /save-vault/ and is excluded from library backups. - Achievement Trail (ADR 0110). Offline RetroAchievements analytics over cache/retroachievements/ : 8-week ISO unlock velocity charts, confidence-rated completion ETAs, next 100-point milestones, cheapest-first next-up queues, and explicit cancellable refresh jobs. - Deal Radar (ADR 0111). Opt-in Steam price watchlist and manual price tracker ( deals_enabled=false by default). Requests and redirects are pinned to https://store.steampowered.com ; polling defaults to 168 hours and price-drop alerts deduplicate per price point. - Player's Log — Time Capsules and Milestone Cards (ADR 0112). Sealed notes and questions stay redacted server-side until a local unlock date, plus nine deterministic milestone kinds with offline 1200x630 PNG share cards. - Backlog Itinerary (ADR 0113). An advisory multi-week play schedule with quick-wins , comeback , and raided strategies, IGDB and own-history completion estimates, RetroAchievements refinement, and live done / on_track / behind / stale status. - Eight new settings and six OpenAPI schemas. save_vault_enabled , save_vault_keep , save_vault_on_close , save_vault_auto_days , deals_enabled , deals_poll_hours , deals_min_drop_pct , and deals_store_cc join the settings registry; docs/openapi.json gains typed schemas for the new surfaces. - Desktop UI and usability polish. body: Enterprise Use this page when you need to verify what you are running. License OpenBox Game Launcher is released under GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. Source is at [vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL](https://github.com/vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL) and the full text is at [LICENSE](https://github.com/vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL/blob/master/LICENSE). Trademark references to LaunchBox, Steam, Heroic, Lutris, RetroArch, and other third party products are used for compatibility description only. See [Legal and trademarks](/policies/legal-and-trademarks/) and [Disclaimer](https://github.com/vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL/blob/master/docs/DISCLAIMER.md). Signed releases Every release is signed with Ed25519. On Linux the installer selects the matching AppImage architecture and verifies the release against a pinned public key and a published SHA-256 checksum. On Windows the release asset install.ps1 runs the same trust ladder: it fetches openbox-release.pub and checks its SHA-256 against a pinned bootstrap anchor (unless -PublicKeyPath is given), then verifies the archive's .sha256 sidecar and its Ed25519 .sig before extracting. Windows installs land under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenBox by default ( -InstallDir or OPENBOX_INSTALL_DIR overrides it), with the previous tree kept at \share\openbox.previous for rollback. On macOS, the signed universal app bundle is verified by install-macos.sh and by the in-app updater, against the same pinned key, SHA-256 checksum, and Ed25519 signature, before anything is installed. The bundle is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS asks you to allow it on first launch. title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about OpenBox, its data, and its limits.
body: Frequently asked questions Does OpenBox include games or ROMs? No. OpenBox does not distribute games, ROMs, BIOS files, firmware, or DRM circumvention tools. You supply the files; OpenBox catalogs, launches, and tracks them. Does it require an online account? No OpenBox account is required. Optional integrations may have their own accounts, credentials, API terms, and rate limits. RetroAchievements and EmuMovies use your existing accounts, and metadata syncing talks to the public LaunchBox Games Database with your consent. What operating systems are supported? OpenBox targets Linux , Windows x86_64 and ARM64 (x86_64 since 1.13.0; ARM64 since 2.0), and macOS 11 or newer on Apple Silicon and Intel (since 1.19.0). - Linux: desktops, laptops, Steam Deck systems, and handheld PCs on x86_64 and aarch64. Release artifacts are built for both architectures — pick the AppImage matching uname -m , and the built-in updater only offers the artifact matching the running architecture. Source builds need Rust 1.92+; packaged builds ship the Rust server with no Python runtime. Python 3.11+ is only for the fallback and .py plugins. - Windows: x86_64 and ARM64 (ARM64 since 2.0), installed from the signed portable package with install.ps1 . Windows PowerShell 5.1 is enough; the installer needs neither curl nor OpenSSL. - macOS: the signed universal app bundle, installed with install-macos.sh into ~/Applications . The bundle ships the Rust openbox-server with no Python runtime and renders the UI in a WKWebView window. The installer needs python3 3.11 or newer on PATH to verify the release. Linux stays the primary distro-integration target. See [Installation](/install/), [Windows](/windows/), and [macOS](/macos/). What are the requirements? The runtime is dependency-free on every platform: standard library only (plus ctypes on Windows), no pip install , no requirements.txt , and no virtualenv. Platform Install Requirements --- --- --- Linux AppImage, Flatpak, or source Rust 1.92+ for source builds; no Python in packaged builds; WebKitGTK for the native window Windows Signed portable package via install.ps1 Windows x86_64 or ARM64, Windows PowerShell 5.1; the WebView2 runtime for the native window (present on Windows 11 and most Windows 10 systems) macOS Signed universal app bundle via install-macos.sh , or source macOS 11 or newer on Apple Silicon or Intel; python3 3.11+ on PATH for the installer; WKWebView is built into macOS Does OpenBox run on Windows? Yes, since 1.13.0. Windows x86_64 and ARM64 install from the signed portable package using the published install.ps1 , which verifies the release key, the archive checksum, and its Ed25519 signature before extracting to %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenBox . The launchers openbox.cmd and openbox.ps1 start the app; --web forces the browser app window. The native window is WebView2: the portable install ships native_host.exe compiled, and a source checkout either drops in the released OpenBox-x86_64-windows-native-host.exe as native

description: Import one local executable and launch it safely.
body: This path is for a first run with a local executable folder. Use a disposable folder if you are testing, so the experiment cannot touch real games. When you start OpenBox for the first time, OpenBoxGL does several things silently: it creates your data directory ( ~/.local/share/openbox-game-launcher on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA%\openbox-game-launcher on Windows, or ~/Library/Application Support/openbox-game-launcher on macOS), generates a per-launch server.token , writes the port to server.port , and initializes an empty library.json with schema version 7. You won't see these files unless you look in the data directory, but they're the reason nothing gets corrupted when the server restarts unexpectedly. See [Interfaces and data](/interfaces-and-data/) for where every file lives. The goal is a full loop: install, import one game, see it in the library, launch it, and confirm the session was recorded. It also proves the data model works: the entry you import is the entry that launches, and the session you play is the session that appears in history. Before you start - Follow [Installation](/install/) and start OpenBox. On Linux, run the AppImage, Flatpak, or source entry point ( ./openbox or ./openbox --web ). On Windows, double-click openbox.cmd or run powershell -File .\openbox.ps1 from the runtime directory; add --web to either one to force the browser app window instead of the native window. On macOS, open OpenBox.app from Applications or run openbox from a terminal. The full Windows path is in [Windows](/windows/), and the macOS path is in [macOS](/macos/). You should see the three-column workspace: filters on the left, an empty cover grid in the center, and the detail pane on the right. - Make one folder containing a single launchable file. On Linux that is an executable .sh file; on Windows use an .exe (or a .cmd / .bat script). For a realistic first test on Linux, use a short script like this: Make it executable ( chmod +x ). On Windows, install.ps1 already placed the runtime under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenBox\share\openbox , so any small .exe on your machine works as the test target. A non-executable file with no launch command is the most common first-launch failure, and the app now reports it explicitly instead of silently failing. title: Arcade Room and Kiosk mode
description: Browse a controller-friendly platform showroom and configure its local kiosk convenience boundary.
body: Arcade Room is a controller-friendly canvas showroom for the library. It groups cabinets by platform, uses available local art and media, and lets you inspect or launch the selected game without leaving the room. Enter and move around Open Tools → 3D arcade room , or choose Arcade Room from the Ctrl/Cmd-K command palette. The current UI controls are: Control Action --- --- Left / Right Walk between cabinets in the current platform zone Up / Down Move between platform zones Home / End Jump to the first/last cabinet Enter Open the selected game's details Space or P Play the selected game M Toggle Kiosk mode Escape or Backspace Close the room Gamepad D-pad/stick navigates; mapped Play, Back, Favorite, and Menu buttons launch, leave, select, and toggle Kiosk mode The room uses the same library and media projections as the main UI. Missing cover art or media produces a labeled placeholder; it is not a promise that every cabinet has artwork. Kiosk mode Kiosk mode (the Museum mode internally) turns the room into a self-guided exhibit. It shows real facts available in the selected game record—such as title, year, developer, genre, play time, and achievement counts—and advances through the room while the exhibit is idle. Any keyboard, pointer, or controller activity exits Kiosk mode. Users with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce receive a static presentation rather than the animation loop. Kiosk PIN The optional Kiosk PIN makes unattended browsing a little less casual. Configure it in Settings → Big Box ( Require a PIN before entering Kiosk mode and Kiosk PIN , 4–12 digits) or through the API: PINs are 4–12 digits. OpenBox stores only a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 digest locally. GET /api/v2/arcade/kiosk/status reports whether the feature is enabled and whether a PIN is set; POST /api/v2/arcade/kiosk/verify returns only . This is a convenience boundary for a local exhibit, not account authentication, network access control, or a security guarantee. The API still requires the normal per-launch token. Clear the PIN with . Entry points and caveats There is no registered openbox://arcade URI in the current parser or SPA. Use Tools or the command palette. openbox://bigbox and ?deeplink=bigbox open Big Box, which is a related fullscreen surface but not a deep link for the Arcade Room itself. MAME set classification ( parent / merged / split / non-merged ) is an import-time property, not a room filter — see [Importing](/guides/library/importing/ arcade-sets) and [Troubleshooting](/guides/troubleshooting/ import-problems). title: Household members, challenges, and sharing
description: Keep optional household records and leaderboards local while exchanging them through a mounted folder.
body: Household is an opt-in local record layer for people who share a library or a play space. It supports members, challenges, challenge results, stat shares, and leaderboard projections without an OpenBox account, hosted multiplayer, or telemetry. Start locally Open Tools → Family sharing (the Household dialog). Add a member with a stable local member_id and display name, then create a challenge with a title, metric, target, and optional participants/game/deadline. Results are records, so another device can validate and merge them rather than receiving an opaque database dump. The core routes are: - GET /api/v2/household?period=daily weekly monthly all_time for records, challenge progress, and the derived leaderboard; - GET /api/v2/household/leaderboard?period=weekly for a leaderboard-focused response; - POST /api/v2/household/member with member_id , display_name , and optional avatar_color / stats_shared ; - POST /api/v2/household/challenge with title , positive target , and optional metric , description , game_id , deadline , and participant_ids ; - POST /api/v2/household/challenge/result with challenge_id , member_id , and a non-negative value ; and - POST /api/v2/household/share with member_id and a period, after stats sharing is enabled. Stats sharing is explicit Household records and play statistics are separate. Leaderboards that use play statistics stay empty or limited until Household stats sharing is enabled. A share request while it is off returns HOUSEHOLD_STATS_DISABLED . This is per-device opt-in; do not enable it on a device whose play history should remain private. Exchange records through a mounted folder Configure the existing mounted cloud sync folder in Settings → Integrations. It can be a local path, Syncthing folder, Nextcloud mount, or another folder that both machines can read. Household does not upload to an OpenBox service. 1. Add or update local members/challenges/results. 2. Use Publish to write pending validated records to the shared folder. 3. On another device, use Pull to read and merge the records. 4. Review the resulting leaderboard and any new challenge progress. The API equivalents are POST /api/v2/household/sync/publish and POST /api/v2/household/sync/pull . POST /api/v2/household/merge accepts a validated record list for a controlled integration, and POST /api/v2/household/record appends a raw record through the same validation boundary. The sync protocol accepts v1 and the current household format; a missing mounted folder is an actionable error, not a fallback to a remote service. What Household does not do Household is deliberately marked partial in the parity matrix. It converges local records and derives leaderboards, but it does not provide hosted accounts, real-time multiplayer, remote notifications, or a vendor cloud. title: Handheld performance
description: Apply optional per-launch handheld performance profiles.
body: Performance profiles apply a TDP limit through ryzenadj before a game launches, and optionally restore a configured value when the session ends. They are per launch profile: either a platform profile or a per-game launch profile override. Handheld performance limits are a Linux feature: they use ryzenadj on Linux only. On Windows and macOS the Handheld performance controls are hidden. Setup Open Tools → Emulators & controllers , create or pick a profile (for example GameCube = dolphin-emu -b -e ), then in the Handheld performance section check Enable TDP , set Limit (W) to your desired cap (e.g. 12 ), and optionally set Restore (W) . Leave Apply handheld performance limits on auto (the default) so the limit applies only in Game Mode or on battery. Install ryzenadj on the host if it is not already present. In Tools → Emulators & controllers , after a profile exists (for example GameCube = dolphin-emu -b -e ), the Handheld performance section lists each profile with: - Enable TDP checkbox - Limit (W) : the TDP applied at launch (0-60, step 0.5) - Restore (W) : the TDP applied when the session ends (0-60, step 0.5) Limits are stored in watts and converted to milliwatts for ryzenadj -stapm-limit= . A profile with only a limit and no restore value applies the limit at launch and does nothing on close. When limits apply The Apply handheld performance limits setting (Settings) has three modes: - auto (default): applies only when OpenBoxGL detects a gamescope guest (Steam Deck / Bazzite game mode) or a battery-powered host ( /sys/class/power_supply/BAT present). - always : applies on any host. - off : never applies. Because auto gates on battery or gamescope, a desktop session never applies or restores a limit. The same gating decides restore, so a session that never applied a limit does not try to restore one. Battery reporting (v1.18.0) Big Box shows a battery indicator in its status bar when a battery is present; Show the battery indicator in Big Box ( battery_indicator , default on) controls it. The indicator uses the browser Battery Status API when available and otherwise calls GET /api/v2/native/battery , which reads the first BAT device under /sys/class/power_supply on Linux, pmset -g batt on macOS, and GetSystemPowerStatus on Windows, and returns present , percent , and charging . A host with no battery returns present: false . This indicator is display-only. The auto performance gate keeps its own battery check and is unaffected by turning the indicator off, so hiding the badge never changes whether a TDP limit applies. Big Box requests the reading when it opens and reuses the 60-second cache, which keeps it off the launch hot path. Failure behavior Missing ryzenadj on PATH, a permission failure, a non-Ryzen CPU, or a malformed TDP value are logged as warnings and do not block the game launch. title: Backlog Radio and query grammar
description: Ask the local library what to play with explainable recommendations, query chips, and the command palette.
body: OpenBox 1.11 adds three local ways to get from “I have too many games” to a defensible next action: Backlog Radio , the deterministic query bar, and the Ctrl/Cmd-K command palette . Backlog Radio Backlog Radio appears in the local Insights/Discovery surface as a playlist of up to five games. Each pick carries reason chips derived from your library and recorded sessions, plus an estimated_minutes field (integer, rounded): the genre-based length estimate minus already-played minutes (floor 15; unplayed games report the full estimate). The model uses a bounded recent history window, session length, genres/platforms, completion patterns, freshness, and related-game signals; it does not call an online recommendation service. It sits alongside the Discovery Center's built-in Games with achievements shelf and any plugin-contributed shelves; see [Discovery](/guides/discovery/). The first recommendations are deliberately modest. The habit model needs enough recorded sessions before it claims to know your habits; otherwise the response carries a fallback notice and uses library freshness/rating signals. Completed, hidden, unavailable, and already selected entries are excluded from a normal backlog pick. Refreshing replaces the managed Backlog Radio selection rather than silently duplicating it. Use Refresh picks when you want a new set, or call: The response is with the picks, explanations, estimated_minutes per pick, and any honest fallback notice. Without enough history the fallback ranks by rating then freshness and reports score: 0.0 . The related abandonment radar is available as GET /api/v2/insights/radar ; its winnable / park entries also carry estimated_minutes . POST /api/v2/insights/radar/park parks a stalled game when you choose to stop seeing it in the radar. Query the collection Type a short phrase in the library search bar. OpenBox parses the phrase with a small deterministic grammar and renders the interpretation as removable chips. Examples include: Query Intended interpretation --- --- short unplayed rpg A game with a short estimate, backlog/never-played progress, and an RPG genre match recently played on Steam A recent play window plus the Steam source co-op for 4 Multiplayer/player-count constraints where the metadata contains the data retro platformer A release-year ceiling plus a platformer genre match The grammar also understands typed terms such as platform:PC , quoted values, negative terms, ratings, progress, time/idle phrases, sources, tags, stores, ESRB, region, series, and player counts. Thresholds are intentionally simple: “short/quick” is at most 5 estimated hours, “long/epic” is at least 20, “highly rated” starts at 4.0, “top rated” at 4.5, and “retro/classic” uses a release year of 2000 or earlier. These are filters, not promises that metadata exists for every game. Unknown words remain ordinary title/metadata text. A phrase is never promoted to a guessed filter just because it sounds plausible, and the chips are the source

title: Deal Radar
description: Opt-in Steam price watchlist and manual price tracker, restricted to store.steampowered.com.
body: Deal Radar (ADR 0111, 3.0) tracks prices for games you are waiting to buy. It is off by default and only talks to https://store.steampowered.com ; it does not use a Steam account, cookies, or telemetry. Enable it Open Tools Deal Radar , or set: Setting Default Meaning --- --- --- deals_enabled false Opt in to the watchlist and price polling. deals_poll_hours 168 Hours between polls, 24-720. deals_min_drop_pct 10 Minimum drop for an alert, 1-90. deals_store_cc "us" Two-letter Steam store country code. 3.0 scheduling note: the Rust server's hourly tick does not currently call deals_due , so the automatic poll does not fire under openbox-server . Use Refresh now ( POST /api/v2/deals/refresh ) until the scheduler is wired. Watch a game From a game's Details pane, choose Deal Radar watch , or call: The watchlist is capped at 200 items and keeps at most 50 price points per item. Unwatch removes the item and purges its history. Manual entry adds a non-Steam title with a price you track yourself. Alerts A price drop at or above deals_min_drop_pct produces one notification. last_notified_price_cents deduplicates, so the same price point does not nag twice, even when the notification feed evicts older entries at its 200-item cap. Network boundary Every request and every HTTP redirect is pinned to https://store.steampowered.com . A redirect to any other host is refused, and the feature sends only the app id or search term plus the store country code. It does not send your library, account, or play history. The [privacy policy](/policies/privacy/) lists Deal Radar as the only scheduled outbound call besides update checks. API Route Behavior --- --- GET /api/v2/deals Watchlist, retained price history, and last-notified prices. GET /api/v2/deals/search Steam store search for a candidate app id. POST /api/v2/deals/watch Add a watched app id. POST /api/v2/deals/unwatch Remove a watch and purge its history. POST /api/v2/deals/entry Add or update a manual entry. POST /api/v2/deals/refresh Poll now. Related pages - [Discovery](/guides/discovery/) - [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/) - [Privacy policy](/policies/privacy/)

title: Discovery
description: Find something to play with the curated Discovery views.
body: The Discovery button (top bar) curates your library into ready-to-play views so you never stare at an empty grid. It works entirely from local library data, no account or network required. Discovery doesn't store pre-computed lists. Each click regenerates the seven built-in views by filtering and sorting against play_count , playtime_seconds , last_played , achievement_sources , and rating, the same counters used for session tracking. That means a game moved from "Continue playing" to the bottom of "Highly rated" the moment it gets marked Completed, without any manual refresh. See [Sessions, saves, and backups](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/) for what feeds these counters. The views View What it shows --- --- Recently added The newest imports Never played Games you have not launched yet Continue playing In-progress games you returned to recently Highly rated Top-rated games in your library Short sessions Games whose past sessions were short, good for a quick play Games with achievements Games that have an achievement set with a total or earned count; includes RetroAchievements, Steam, and plugin sources Random picks A rotating set of surprise titles Each view lists up to 12 games and is regenerated as the library changes. Games with achievements uses the same achievement_sources totals the achievement tabs show, then sorts by RetroAchievements progress and name, so a game does not need a RetroAchievements match to appear. Enabled discovery plugins add their own shelves to the same dialog. A plugin may publish up to ten lists of up to 50 game ids each; they appear under their declared names, and a failing plugin is skipped rather than breaking the built-in views. The response keys are plugin: : , with labels in discovery_names . Explorer rail The Explorer panel in the sidebar breaks your library down by metadata facets: - Dimensions : Genre, Developer, Publisher, Platform, Progress state, and ESRB rating. - Dynamic Counts : Shows how many games match each value (e.g. Platformer (24) , Capcom (12) ). - Compound Filters : Clicking a facet immediately applies a scoped search query to your library view. - REST API : Backed by GET /api/v2/explorer/facets?field= , returning the top 40 sorted facets. Related games and recommendations When viewing any game's detail modal or pane, OpenBox dynamically computes the most relevant titles in your collection: - Scoring Engine : Evaluates similarity weights across shared series (+5), developer (+3), publisher (+2), genre (+2), collection (+2), and platform (+1). - Reason Badges : Badges explain why each game was recommended (e.g. Same Series , Same Developer , Shared Genre ). - API Endpoint : Accessible via GET /api/v2/related/rich?id= or ?game_id= . See also - [Library overview](/guides/library/), browsing and filtering the full library - [API content and imports](/reference/api/content-and-imports/), GET /api/v2/discovery - [API local administrator](/reference/api/local-admin/), GET /api/v2/explorer/facets

title: Emulators and launching
description: Configure profiles, tokens, archives, dependencies, and session controls.
body: OpenBoxGL launches games through tokenized commands, never shell interpolation. A launch command is split with shell rules into an argument list, and tokens are replaced per argument; a path with spaces stays one argument. Launching is a fixed sequence, resolve path → extract archive → resolve command → substitute tokens → apply perf → run before_launch plugins → spawn → track → after_session . The full order and where each validation error fires is documented in [How OpenBoxGL works](/reference/how-it-works/ the-launch-pipeline). Knowing the order tells you exactly which step a failure came from. Profiles The Emulators & controllers entry in the Tools menu opens the Emulator profiles dialog (and the install catalog described below). Profiles are one per line: Platform = command . Tokens available in any command: Token Value --- --- / / Absolute game or ROM path (after archive extraction, when enabled) / Game title / Parent directory of the target game file / Filename with extension / Filename without extension ROM filename / Platform name Emulator parent directory OpenBox data directory path Steam application ID Heroic application ID Lutris game identifier The core file name the game uses, already expanded from the definition or your per-game/per-platform choice / / / Quick Resume state values from the adapter state: block ( crates/openbox-emulators/src/tokens.rs ); empty for ordinary launch commands If a profile command has no and the game has no per-game command, the resolved path is appended. A .sh game with no command launches with bash ; otherwise the path itself runs when it is executable. Launch Precedence Hierarchy When launching a title, OpenBox resolves the executable and arguments using a strict 5-level hierarchy (ADR 0012): 1. Per-Game Launch Command : Explicit command configured in Edit metadata ( launch ). 2. Per-Game Selected Adapter/Profile : Profile override set on the game entry ( emulator_adapter_id or emulator_id ). 3. Platform-Level Profile : User-configured platform profile in Emulator Profiles. 4. Authoritative Adapter Registry : Auto-detected matching adapter from emulator_defs/ ( GET /api/v2/emulators/registry ). 5. Direct Executable Fallback : Native binary execution if target file has executable permissions ( +x ). A platform-level override ( settings.emulator_platform_settings ) sits across levels 2 and 3: it supplies an adapter id only when the game has none, a RetroArch core only when the game has none, and extra arguments that are always appended. See [Per-platform emulator overrides]( per-platform-emulator-overrides). A per-game launch_profile chooses which named profile is used as the platform command. Emulator catalog The same dialog lists supported emulators with install state, mode (native or Flatpak), platforms, and per-platform profiles (44 adapter YAML files in emulator_defs/ , covering 19 emulators): - FS-UAE (Amiga ) - Azahar (Nintendo 3DS ) - Cemu (Wii U -g ) - Dolphin (GameCube, Wii, WiiWare, all -b -e

title: Steam Bridge and ES-DE migration
description: Move handheld library entries with reviewable Steam shortcuts.vdf and ES-DE gamelist workflows.
body: OpenBox provides two review-first migration paths for handheld users: Steam Bridge writes only OpenBox-owned entries to Steam's shortcuts.vdf , and ES-DE import reads a bounded gamelist.xml into the local catalog. Steam Bridge Steam Bridge can find a recent shortcuts.vdf under the standard Steam userdata roots, or you can pass an explicit absolute path . It parses the file losslessly enough to preserve unrelated records and builds a plan containing additions, updates, removals, unchanged entries, and a source fingerprint. Use the API in two phases: Review the returned plan, then send it back to POST /api/v2/steambridge/apply with the same path. Removal follows the same pattern: POST /api/v2/steambridge/remove/preview with targets , then POST /api/v2/steambridge/remove with the reviewed removal plan. If the file changes between preview and apply, Steam Bridge returns a stale-plan conflict and leaves it untouched. Foreign Steam shortcuts are not OpenBox-owned and are preserved. The status route, GET /api/v2/steambridge/status , reports the selected path, availability, OpenBox count, foreign count, and parse errors without exposing shortcut contents. Limit game_ids to the entries you intend to manage; the route caps the list and requires an absolute path when one is supplied. Launch from Game Mode Bridge entries use the installed openbox launcher. openbox --play accepts a stable OpenBox game_id or numeric library id, starts/uses the local authenticated server, and dispatches the same launch path as the UI. It does not copy game files or bypass Steam/emulator launch profiles. See [Command line and deep links](/reference/cli/) for the CLI and [Steam Deck and handhelds](/steam-deck/) for --game-mode . ES-DE gamelist import Open Tools → Artwork & details (the LaunchBox Games Database dialog) and use the ES-DE import section: choose the gamelist.xml , press Preview ES-DE import , review the report, then Apply preview . You can also call the v2 routes directly: the request takes an absolute xml_path (the gamelist key is accepted as an alias) and optional options such as path mappings and overwrite choices. Always preview first: The preview parses the gameList XML, normalizes identity and metadata, maps supported media fields, reports counts/operations, and returns source digests plus a preview token. Review the additions and merges, then send the plan and token to POST /api/v2/import/esde/apply . The source XML, the OpenBox base state, and the reviewed plan are all checked again; a changed file or library produces ESDE_STALE_PLAN before mutation. The parser is intentionally bounded and rejects a missing file, malformed XML, an unexpected root, or an oversized source. It preserves local path identity and does not silently install an emulator or rewrite launch commands. Configure the emulator profile separately; Vita3K and Xenia are in the current emulator catalog, and both currently declare no Quick Resume state capability. See [Library importing](/guides/

title: Faugus Launcher Integration
description: Import Faugus Launcher games and their prefixes, with suggested UMU launch commands.
body: OpenBox provides native integration with Faugus Launcher , the lightweight Linux game manager for Wine and UMU games: it reads Faugus manifests and prefixes and imports the titles into your unified library. Overview Faugus Launcher is a Linux launcher, so this integration is Linux only. On Windows and macOS the scanner finds nothing and its controls are hidden. When Faugus Launcher is installed, OpenBox can scan its data directories, read each game's prefix configuration, and import the titles into your unified library. OpenBox looks for Faugus data in ~/.config/faugus-launcher , ~/.local/share/faugus-launcher , ~/Faugus , the matching XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME locations, and prefix directories containing drive_c . How to Import from Faugus 1. Open Add games in the top bar and choose Guided setup… (the Setup Center, headed "Set up your library"). 2. On the Sources step, add the Faugus source. 3. Continue to the scan: OpenBox detects all titles defined in Faugus manifests and prefix directories as preview candidates. 4. Review and commit the preview as usual. You can also drive the scan entirely through the REST API (below). Each imported title automatically receives: - Cross-source identity deduplication (a title already in the library from another source is merged rather than added twice) - Target executable path - Dedicated Wine prefix path, recorded as wine_prefix - A suggested launch command ( umu-run ) — a starting point you can edit in Edit Metadata, not a wrapper the app applies for you. Prefix-only rows import without it. REST Endpoints Automate Faugus scans or integrate with scripts: - GET /api/v2/faugus/status : Reports whether Faugus data directories exist, and which ones. - GET /api/v2/faugus/scan : Scans manifests and prefix directories and returns the discovered games with their prefix and runner metadata. - POST /api/v2/faugus/import : Imports the scanned games into the OpenBox library.

title: Backlog management
description: Track progress, personal ratings, playtime, and notes for every game.
body: Every game carries a personal backlog layer on top of its progress field: statuses, your own star rating, logged play sessions, and dated notes. All of it feeds pickers, filters, search grammar, and exports. Progress statuses The progress field holds the canonical statuses, and an unset progress renders as Unplayed everywhere — cards, details, badges, explorer facets, and filters. progress:unplayed is a first-class search clause. The set of labels offered is configurable in Settings → Sessions & Saves → Progress values allowed by automation and the game editor (default Unplayed, Playing, Paused, Beaten, Completed, Mastered, Abandoned): the game editor and progress automation only offer enabled labels, and the API rejects a label that is not on the list. The legacy single-string notes never silently change progress: the optional one-time Mark as Playing? prompt appears on first launch for unplayed games, with a settings kill switch and per-game prompted-once persistence — it never sets progress silently. Personal ratings Your own star rating ( user_rating , 0–5, where 0 is unrated) is separate from the metadata rating that comes from providers. Hover star widgets on cards and in the details pane set it; card badges show it, My rating is a sort option and a bulk-edit field, and the game picker weights highly-rated unplayed games with a composite reason (e.g. "rated 4 stars, never started it, ~12h to beat"). Search it with the smart grammar: my 4 stars , unrated by me , myrating:4 . Manual playtime Log sessions from the details pane with a date, seconds, and a note; entries can be edited or deleted. Playtime stats and totals include manual time, while streaks still count observed sessions only. Exports carry the manual fields. Dated notes Notes are stored as timestamped entries — legacy single-string notes migrate to this shape on read, with no bulk rewrite. Add, edit, and delete notes from the details pane. Progress, ratings, playtime, and notes all have v2 routes under /api/v2/library/progress/ , /api/v2/library/rating/ , /api/v2/library/playtime/ , and /api/v2/library/notes/ ; the v1 surface is frozen. See [API reference](/reference/api/).

title: Library export
description: Export your library, or a platform/playlist scope of it, to JSON or CSV with shareable-by-construction field projection.
body: OpenBox can export your library to JSON or CSV — for migrations between machines, auditing your collection in a spreadsheet, or sharing a view of it. Queue an export 1. Open Settings → Advanced → Export library (or queue it through the API with POST /api/v2/library/export ). 2. Pick the format : JSON (full field projection) or CSV (spreadsheet-friendly). 3. Pick the scope : the whole library ( all ), a single platform, or a playlist. 4. Optionally include media paths (off by default). The export runs as a durable job in the Activity Center — you can cancel it, and it survives an app restart. Shareable by construction Exports contain only the game-field projection. Settings, credentials, webhooks, and history are never included, so an export is safe to share as-is. Media paths are opt-in because they leak directory layout. Files and rotation Exports land in /exports/ with collision-safe filenames. The newest 10 exports are kept; older ones are removed automatically. List them with GET /api/v2/library/export/exports ( crates/openbox-http/src/handlers/export.rs ), download them from the export dialog (validated by name regex and directory containment), or fetch one with GET /api/v2/library/export/download?file= &token= — the session token is the same one the UI appends to its own download link. Note the export download uses ?file= , while the backup diff below uses ?archive= . To compare the live library against a backup archive (not an export file), use GET /api/v2/backup/diff?archive= ( crates/openbox-http/src/handlers/health.rs ): it reports added / removed / changed game ids plus settings_changed and a summary . Only OpenBoxBackup- .zip archives inside the data directory or backups/ are accepted. See also - [API: ScreenScraper and export](/reference/api/screenscraper-and-export/) for the exact endpoints - [Library backups](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/library-backups/) for whole-library archives (a different feature: backups restore, exports are for data-out) - [Background jobs](/reference/background-jobs/) for the durable job lifecycle

title: Importing
description: Bring storefronts, executables, ROMs, and arcade sets into one catalog.
body: OpenBoxGL imports from installed storefront manifests, local ROM folders, standalone executables, and arcade DAT catalogs. Every importer reports how many games were found and added; entries that already exist are skipped, so re-running an import never creates duplicates. Imported games keep a stable identity (Steam App ID, Heroic App ID, Lutris ID, Gameyfin ID, GOG/EA/Ubisoft provider ID, or path) so later imports merge into the existing entry instead of adding a second copy. Each imported game gets a game_id derived from a SHA-256 over its identity (normalized path, platform, and store ids). The importer computes the same hash on every run, so a game that already exists is recognized and updated, not duplicated. This is also why a game keeps its sessions, saves, queue entries, and history when you reorder or re-import. See [How OpenBoxGL works](/reference/how-it-works/ the-state-store) for the identity model. Library Setup Center (Recommended) Click Add games → Guided setup… in the top bar to launch the guided Library Setup Center . Its quick path is six steps — Where are your games? , Check what we found , Review matches , Choose emulators , Import games , You're done — with Welcome and Artwork & details available behind Show advanced options : 1. Preview Before Commit : Setup Center performs a read-only scan of folders and storefronts ( POST /api/v2/setup/preview ). No changes are written to library.json until you approve them. 2. Storytelling Progress : Scans report discovered games, platforms, and actionable decision counts. 3. Paginated Review & Candidate Resolution : Review discovered titles in batches ( GET /api/v2/setup/preview/items ). Resolve shared extensions (e.g. .iso matching PS2 or GameCube) with your chosen platform/emulator. 4. Idempotent Commit : Confirm your choices ( POST /api/v2/setup/commit ). Imported games receive a unique import_batch_id for instant post-import filtering and batch metadata review. Direct Folder Import Click Add games → Scan a folder… (or Add one game… for a single entry) and select an absolute path. OpenBoxGL scans recursively by extension and assigns a platform from the extension table: - .nes NES, .sfc / .smc SNES, .gba Game Boy Advance, .gb Game Boy, .gbc Game Boy Color, .n64 / .z64 / .v64 Nintendo 64, .nds Nintendo DS, .3ds / .cia Nintendo 3DS, .wbfs / .wia / .wad Wii / WiiWare, .rvz / .gcm / .gcz GameCube, .xci / .nsp Nintendo Switch, .pbp PSP, .vpk PlayStation Vita, .xex Xbox 360, .cue / .chd / .ciso / .m3u Disc image - .sh , .appimage , .exe , .rom , .zip , .7z , .rar also import as-is. Ambiguous Extension Resolution Per ADR 0012, shared disc extensions (such as .iso ) no longer guess platforms silently. OpenBox flags ambiguous multi-platform extensions ( AMBIGUOUS_PLATFORM ) and presents explicit platform candidates for user resolution in Setup Center and the launch check. title: Library overview
description: Browse, search, and safely maintain a mixed-platform game library.
body: OpenBoxGL presents imported games in a searchable grid or list. Select a card to open its detail pane, where metadata, artwork, launch, saves, and history stay together. The 3.0 workspace The 3.0 redesign puts games above the fold. The sticky library header is a single 94 px row; Artwork and Layout live in a Display popover, Settings sits directly in the top bar, and the Tools menu has a Filter tools… field and a 3-column layout that fits all 41 entries at 1440x900. The drag-and-drop banner stays hidden until you drag files over the window, Jump back in is a slim dismissible strip, and the empty right Details pane auto-collapses until you select a game or collection. Close Details with its x button or Escape . The sidebar is ordered Search , View , Platforms , Categories , Playlists , and a collapsed More filters section (ESRB, Source, Exclude, Explorer). Game Details keeps four primary actions upfront and folds More actions , Save management , and Launch check into collapsible cards; Launch check expands on its own only when an issue needs attention. Surprise me is a one-click instant pick, while the What should I play? picker remains available for constraint-scored picks. The top bar is grouped into three zones: - The Library zone holds Library and one Add games menu ( addMenuButton ) that gathers every way in: Add one game… , Scan a folder… , Add a game without files… , Guided setup… , and the store shortcuts Steam , Heroic , Lutris , and More game stores… . Guided setup opens the [Setup Center](/guides/library/setup-center/). - The Actions zone holds Big Box , Running now , Play queue , and Activity ( activityButton with live running operation count). - The Tools menu ( toolsButton ) is organized into four accessible WAI-ARIA groups, each entry carrying a one-line hint: 1. title: Play Insights
description: Local-first gameplay analytics, 366-day activity heatmap, streaks, and momentum tracking with zero telemetry.
body: OpenBox 1.9.0 introduced the built-in, local-first Play Insights dashboard, still shipped in 1.18.0. It turns your recorded play sessions into meaningful analytics without external services, accounts, or telemetry. Features - 366-Day Playtime Heatmap : Visual activity grid (53 weeks x 7 days) color-coded across 5 intensity levels (0 to 4) reflecting your daily playtime. - Streaks & Momentum : Real-time calculation of current daily streak, longest streak, and 30-day playtime momentum (comparing the last 30 days vs the preceding 30 days). - Top Platforms & Genres : Aggregated playtime rankings across your collection. - What it cost (v1.17.0) : Price-paid totals grouped by currency, plus cost per hour and best/worst value for priced games with at least one minute played. No conversion is performed. - Strict Privacy : Computed on the fly from local session history ( history in library.json ) and cached in memory. Opening Play Insights 1. Open OpenBox and stay on the library. 2. Scroll past the grid: Play Insights is the last section on the page and loads the first time it comes into view. 3. The header carries a Wrapped button, a range selector (30, 90, or 365 days), a refresh button, and a collapse toggle that is remembered between visits. The panel appears only once the library has games, and the Show Play Insights in the library checkbox in Settings (Library or Appearance) hides it. What it cost (v1.17.0) Open a game's edit dialog and enter Price paid and its Currency . The default currency for new prices comes from Settings → Library ( currency , a three-letter code; USD by default). Bulk Edit can set or clear a price for several games at once. The What it cost card shows one row per currency with the total, the number of priced games, total hours, and cost per hour. It also lists the five best- and five worst-value games. A rate appears only when the game cost money and has at least one minute of playtime; a zero price or an unplayed game has no rate. There is no exchange-rate source and no conversion. Two currencies are shown as two separate totals, never added together. Price paid, currency, and the derived rates stay on the device and do not cross the library-sync protocol; Time Machine does not journal price changes. The data is part of the existing summary response at GET /api/v2/insights/summary under spend : ], "best_value": [...], "worst_value": [...]} . cost_per_hour_cents is null when no rate applies. Design System Tokens The Play Insights heatmap and cards use dedicated design tokens: - --overlay-insight-cell-0 : Inactive / zero-playtime cell background - --overlay-insight-cell-1 through --overlay-insight-cell-4 : Stepped playtime intensity levels - --border-insight : Heatmap grid and stat card borders - --shadow-insight : Elevated insight card shadows - --surface-insight-card : Card background surface API Endpoints - GET /api/v2/insights/summary : High-level analytics summary (total playtime, session count, active streaks, top platfo

title: Backlog Itinerary
description: An advisory multi-week play schedule with quick-wins, comeback, and raided strategies.
body: Backlog Itinerary (ADR 0113, 3.0) turns an unfinished library into a capacity-bounded play schedule. It is advisory: it does not change progress or launch games for you. Build a plan Open Tools Backlog Itinerary , or call POST /api/v2/itinerary/plan . Inputs: - Horizon — 7 to 365 days. - Pace — 5 to 960 minutes per day. - Strategy — quick-wins (shortest first), comeback (games you have already started), or raided (prioritize RetroAchievements progress). The response returns entries (scheduled games with an estimate), later (games that did not fit), and capacity_hours . How estimates are made 1. IGDB time-to-beat, when the game has an IGDB match. The lookup is a bounded concurrency-2 job and is cached under cache/igdb/ . 2. Own history median completion time, when you have at least 3 completed samples for comparable games. 3. Labeled default of 8.0 hours when neither is available. 4. RetroAchievements progress refines the remaining estimate when a matching cache exists. The plan shows which source produced each estimate. Live status Each entry is done , on_track , behind , or stale . The status is derived from elapsed days, your playtime since the plan started, and the estimate. A completed entry is pinned; Replan rebuilds around it. Abandon clears the active plan. The plan is stored in state["itinerary"] ; deleting it loses only the schedule, not progress. Related pages - [Library](/guides/library/) - [Backlog](/guides/library/backlog/) - [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/)

title: Library navigation
description: Keyboard and gamepad navigation across the library grid and list, hash routing for shareable links, and the screenshot lightbox.
body: Since OpenBox 1.8.0, the library grid and list view support full keyboard and gamepad navigation, plus hash routing so any library view can be shared or bookmarked. Keyboard navigation - Arrow keys / Home / End / Page Up / Page Down move the focus across the grid or list; scrolling is virtualization-aware, so focus reveal works in 50k-game libraries. - f toggles favorite on the focused game; Escape clears the current selection. - Enter opens the focused game's detail pane. - F1 or ? opens Help & shortcuts — Start here, the glossary, and the shortcut table — unless focus is in a text field or a dialog is already open. Gamepad and the controller map Gamepad input runs through a configurable controller map (Settings → Controller). Each mapped action ( play , back , favorite , random , page_left , page_right , pause , menu ) can be bound to a button number (0–31) with edge detection, so held buttons don't repeat. The controller bench tab visualizes live gamepad input so you can verify bindings without launching a game. Hash routing The library view is encoded in the URL as /key/value hash fragments — platform, category, playlist, filter preset, search query ( q ), selected game, sort state, and the include/exclude filter pairs. Refreshing restores exactly where you were, including filters you excluded rather than selected, and copying the address bar gives someone a link that opens the same view. No server round-trip is involved; the fragments are read and written locally. Sidebar order and sections Settings → Library has a Sidebar section order list with up/down buttons for search, view, filters, platforms, playlists, and explorer, so the parts you use can sit at the top, plus a Hidden sidebar sections fieldset of checkboxes; hiding Explorer removes the facet panel entirely. Both are saved as sidebar_sections and hidden_sidebar_sections , and an older saved order that still names a section a later build dropped is accepted instead of being rejected on save. Sortable list columns In list view, click a column header (Title, Platform, Genre, Rating) to cycle the sort direction. ESRB, Progress, and Plays are static display columns. The choice persists via the list_sort and list_sort_dir settings. Screenshot lightbox Open a game's screenshots to view them in a lightbox with previous/next navigation, zoom, and a position counter. Cover art shows a skeleton shimmer while loading. Mood Match adaptive theming (v1.9.0) When mood_match_enabled is on, selecting a game tints the surrounding UI from its cover palette ( applyMoodForGame in static/mood.js:172 ); Big Box follows only when its own mood toggle is also on. Without a cover — or with the toggle off — the theme stays neutral. See [Discovery](/guides/discovery/) for the picker surfaces that pair with it. See also - [Library overview](/guides/library/) for browsing and filters - [Big Box and handhelds](/guides/big-box-and-handhelds/) for fullscreen controller use - [Shortcuts reference](/reference/shortcuts

title: Organizing
description: Use search, filters, collections, playlists, and safe library operations.
body: OpenBoxGL organizes a large catalog through favorites, collections, saved filters, ordered manual playlists, custom fields, ESRB filters, platform categories, and bulk edits. Bulk Edit changes only the fields you specify, missing keys are preserved unchanged. favorite and hidden must be booleans; progress must be a known status; rating is clamped to 0-5. Tags have their own replace/add/remove actions (see [Queue, tags, and notifications](/guides/library/queue-tags-notifications/)) because combining tag replacement with add or remove in one request would be ambiguous. Filters and views The sidebar View selector covers All games, Favorites, Recently played, Never played, In progress, Completed, Installed only, Owned / not installed, Has saves, Hidden, and Missing files. The ESRB filter narrows to E, E10+, T, M, AO, RP, or Unrated. Categories group platforms into Nintendo, Sony, Microsoft, Computer, Arcade, Adventure, and Other by default, overridable in Settings. Explorer facets count and filter by genre, developer, publisher, platform, progress, and ESRB with up to 40 values per field; clicking a facet applies it, and an "Unset"/"Unrated" label covers empty values. Save Filter stores the current platform, category, view, search query, ESRB, and progress as a playlist-style rule set. Save Preset does the same but keeps the rules as a filter preset , optionally pinned as a Big Box quick preset (marked with a star in the sidebar, selectable from the Big Box Filter and Sort menu). Both appear in the sidebar; presets restore their rules when clicked and can be deleted with the × button. Platform and category filters cycle through three states — include, exclude, clear — on repeated clicks. The Source filter is a dropdown with a separate Exclude checkbox, and a smart collection loads its saved query into the search box rather than cycling. Excluded values show as "Not : " chips and are written to the URL hash, so a refresh restores the exclusions along with the rest of the view. Presets and playlists accept more than the sidebar controls expose: source , achievements-source , and region rules, plus a text operator ( contains_any / not_contains_any ) for genre, developer, publisher, and region. Every rule key except view and platform_category can also appear in an exclude block, which rejects matching games rather than adding them — up to 20 values per field, and a refresh keeps the block intact. Visual chip builder (v1.7.2+) Filter presets render as visual chips — compact badges showing the field, operator, and value for each rule (e.g. platform = SNES , genre contains RPG , favorite = true ). Chips are generated from the underlying JSON rules via rules_to_chips() and convert back via chips_to_rules() with round-trip fidelity, so editing a chip and saving produces the same rule structure as before. This makes complex collections with many rules easier to scan and edit at a glance. Playlists Open the Playlists dialog for New manual playlist and New filte

title: Player's Log — Time Capsules and Milestone Cards
description: Sealed notes to your future self, plus nine deterministic milestone cards with PNG export.
body: Player's Log (ADR 0112, 3.0) has two halves: Time Capsules , sealed notes and questions that unlock on a date you choose, and Milestone Cards , deterministic snapshots of library and play milestones that export as 1200x630 PNGs. Time Capsules Open Player's Log from the Tools menu, or use a game's Seal a memory action. A capsule has a kind of note or question , a body of up to 4,000 characters, and an unlock date. - The body stays redacted server-side until the unlock date. GET /api/v2/capsules returns locked entries without their body. - Unlocking happens once at local midnight on the unlock date. The Rust server's hourly tick calls unlock_due_capsules ; opened_at is durable, so a missed tick does not reopen or lose the capsule. - game_id is display metadata, not a foreign key: deleting a game keeps its capsules. Milestone Cards GET /api/v2/insights/milestones returns nine deterministic milestone kinds with binary-searched crossing dates: 1. Playtime total 2. First clear 3. RetroAchievements points 4. Active-week streak 5. Library age 6. Collection size 7. Completed games 8. Mastered games 9. A game-specific playtime milestone The card renderer is offline and shared with Moments. It draws a 1200x630 PNG using your active theme's tokens, so the card matches the app. Export from the milestone card or save the PNG directly. State and storage time_capsules is a top-level library.json collection. Capsule bodies are not included in the public library projection while locked. Milestone cards are derived on demand; the only stored state is the capsule collection. Related pages - [Library](/guides/library/) - [Play Insights](/guides/library/insights/) - [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/)

title: Queue, tags, and notifications
description: Manage the persistent play queue, normalized tags, notifications, and webhooks.
body: OpenBox's Queue, Tags, Notifications, and Webhooks dialogs open from the top bar — Play queue in the Actions zone, and Tags , Notifications , and Webhooks in the Tools menu. All of them are persistent local state stored in the library file (schema version 7). The queue is capped at 500 entries ( play_queue.py CAP = 500 ), notifications at 200 , and webhook configs at 32 ( automation.py MAX_WEBHOOKS = 32 ). A full webhook queue drops the event with a failure notification rather than blocking your library, this prevents a misconfigured webhook from grinding the server to a halt. See [How OpenBoxGL works](/reference/how-it-works/ the-webhook-dispatcher) for the delivery pipeline. Play queue Open Queue to see the queue, Play next , Add selected game , and a Remove button per entry. The queue is capped at 500 entries , each note is limited to 200 characters , and entries are stored by stable game ID so they survive reordering and library edits. - Enqueue adds games at the end (or at a requested position) with an optional note. - Advance (Play next) walks forward, skipping entries whose game is missing or whose path no longer exists; those entries are marked skip and left in place. It returns the next playable entry or null when the queue is exhausted. - Reorder requires the full ordered list of current entry IDs and rejects partial lists. - Remove deletes the given entries. Missing games resolve to a "Missing" label with the entry retained so you can remove it. Tags Tags are canonicalized: trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, case-insensitively deduplicated (first spelling wins), up to 50 tags per game and 64 characters per tag . Over-long tags raise an error rather than being silently truncated. - Replace sets the full tag list. - Add appends only labels not already present (case-insensitive). - Remove deletes exact case-insensitive matches, preserving order. - Replace and adjust cannot be combined in one request; adding and removing the same label in one request is rejected. The Tags dialog lists tag counts (visible, non-hidden games only, sorted by count then name). Clicking a tag filters the library with a tag: search. Save tags on selected game writes comma-separated tags to the currently selected game. Notifications The Notification Center stores up to 200 entries , newest first. Titles are capped at 200 characters, bodies at 2000. The unread count is fetched at boot, so the Tools menu badge is right without opening the center. Notifications are deduplicated within 10 minutes when the kind and title match, or immediately when an explicit dedupe_key matches (webhook delivery failures reuse a per-event key). Mark all read and Clear act on the whole list or selected IDs. Webhook delivery failures surface here as error-level notifications so you can notice them without polling. Since 1.17.0, notices raised by the server — cloud sync results, launch-check changes, rejected emulator-definition packs, and webhook failures — also carry title_key , body_key ,

title: Library Setup Center
description: Guided first-run setup with non-destructive scan previews, candidate resolution, and safe commits.
body: The Library Setup Center ( setupLibraryButton , reached from Add games → Guided setup… ) provides a safe, guided workflow for importing games, checking emulator readiness, and resolving multi-platform ambiguities before altering your library. It opens on a six-step quick path numbered sequentially 1-6 and leaves two expert stages behind a Show advanced options toggle, so a first run never starts with a dashboard to interpret. Continue stays disabled until at least one source is selected. Workflow Stepper The quick path is Where are your games? → Check what we found → Review matches → Choose emulators → Import games → You're done . Welcome and Artwork & details appear only when Show advanced options is on; turning it off returns to the quick path at the Sources step. The stepper shows the current step as Step N of 6 (or of 8 with advanced options) and a one-line explanation of what the step does. 1. Welcome (advanced): Reviews library health and recommends the next step. 2. Sources : Choose game directories, ROM folders, or installed storefronts (Folder, Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Gameyfin, plus the secondary sources such as Faugus). 3. Check what we found (Scan): OpenBox performs a read-only inspection ( POST /api/v2/setup/preview ), generating a transient preview document identified by preview_id at revision 1. The scanner reports discovered files and highlights items needing your decision. 4. Review matches (Decisions): Review items in batches ( GET /api/v2/setup/preview/items with the preview_id / revision cursor), inspect version candidates and per-candidate emulator_choices , resolve ambiguities, and set platform overrides via decisions. The items cursor is bound to one preview revision — a stale cursor stops with PREVIEW_STALE . 5. Choose emulators (Readiness): the launch check preflight checks ( POST /api/v2/launch/preflight for one game, POST /api/v2/launch/preflight/batch for many) flag missing emulators or missing BIOS files with one-click fix buttons. 6. Artwork & details (Options, advanced): Set metadata, media, region, and import behavior for the commit. 7. Import games (Confirm): Optionally Revalidate preview ( setup.revalidate ) to re-scan sources against the current library — this bumps the preview revision and marks it revalidated — then Continue commits the reviewed plan ( POST /api/v2/setup/commit with preview_id , revision , and decisions). All imported items are tagged with an import_batch_id for easy filtering. Since 1.16.0 the Confirm step also counts the candidates still waiting on a decision : a game the wizard could not resolve is left undecided rather than imported on a guess, so the server's unresolved-candidate guard applies and nothing enters your library that the wizard said needed your attention. 8. You're done (Finish): Shows a completion summary (added, merged, skipped, unmatched, media/launch readiness, warnings, failed) with actions to view imported games, review unmatched metadata, fix launch blockers, or open the

title: Library Time Machine
description: Browse the local journal, inspect a bounded past view, and preview safe catalog reverts.
body: The Time Machine makes catalog history visible without replacing the canonical library. It reads the local journal, reconstructs bounded views, and turns a possible undo into a reviewable plan before anything is written. Open the timeline Choose Tools → Library history , then use Timeline to browse retained events. Filter by days, event kind, or game. Events can include catalog edits, imports, deletes/restores, sessions, and Moments. The journal is local and may be enabled even when catalog synchronization is off. History is bounded by the journal's retained snapshots and events. The journal keeps at most 25,000 events ( JOURNAL_MAX_EVENTS ) over a 400-day retention window ( JOURNAL_RETENTION_DAYS in crates/openbox-sync/src/time_machine.rs ), compacting to a horizon when over budget. If compaction created a horizon, a gap, or a corruption marker, the UI reports that boundary; it does not invent the missing state. Use [Library backups](/reference/library-backups/) when you need a complete archive of files and settings. Browse as of a date The Browse as of tab materializes a read-only catalog view for a date. It is useful for answering “what did my library look like then?” without changing the current library. The view reconstructs catalog metadata and history only; it does not restore media binaries, emulator installations, launch files, or save files. Price-paid and currency changes are not journaled in 1.17.0, so they do not appear as diffs or revert candidates; use [Library backups](/reference/library-backups/) when a price history matters. Compare two points in time The Compare tab (v1.15.0) answers a different question from Browse as of : instead of showing you one point, it shows you the difference between two . Pick one date or two, and the tab lists: - Added — games that exist at the later point and not the earlier one. - Removed — games that existed at the earlier point and not the later one. - Changed — games present at both points whose fields differ, listed field by field so you can see what moved rather than only that something did. Truer numbers than the page shows: the response carries the real totals, so a truncated page reads "showing 200 of 1,340" rather than implying the 200 is everything. If you pick a start date that predates the kept history, the tab says so instead of presenting a partial diff as a complete one. Compare is read-only . It writes nothing and cannot change the library; to go back to a past state you still use a reviewed revert, which stays exactly as bounded as it was. The API equivalent takes the later date as after and accepts an optional earlier before , a fields list, and a limit : Preview a revert From an event, choose the revert action and review the affected game and fields. The request accepts an undo flag to reverse an event's effect rather than re-apply named fields ( crates/openbox-http/src/handlers/timemachine.rs ). title: Media providers
description: Set up IGDB, LaunchBox Games Database, SteamGridDB, ScreenScraper, EmuMovies, Bezel Project, Steam, GOG, and plugin media.
body: OpenBoxGL enriches games from several optional media and metadata providers. This page is the setup guide; the [Accounts and media](/integrations/accounts-and-media/) reference has the exact credentials and API details. Four providers require no credentials and work out of the box: LaunchBox Games Database (public download), Steam (per App ID), GOG (embedded data), and Bezel Project (GitHub public repo). IGDB, ScreenScraper, and SteamGridDB need credentials in ~/.env (optional provider tokens can also be saved in the app — see below). Only EmuMovies requires a paid licensed account. Plugin providers carry their own requirements. All other providers are optional, your library functions perfectly with zero media providers configured. Choose your providers Provider What it provides Credentials needed --- --- --- LaunchBox Games Database Metadata + box front, background, screenshots, box back/spine/3D, clear logo, fanart, banner, icon, title screen, cart fronts/backs, disc, ads/flyers None (public download, up to 2 GiB) IGDB Metadata (name, description, year, genre, developer, publisher, rating, time-to-beat) IGDB_CLIENT_ID + IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET in ~/.env Steam Name, developer, publisher, genre, year, description + cover and header None (per-Steam-App-ID) GOG Cover + background for Heroic/GOG entries None EmuMovies Covers, box backs/spines/3D boxes, screenshots, title screens, marquees, cart fronts/backs, discs, clear logos, snap and theme videos, manuals, music Licensed account ( EMUMOVIES_USERNAME / EMUMOVIES_PASSWORD ) SteamGridDB Covers, backgrounds, clear logos, icons, banners STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY in ~/.env Bezel Project Per-platform bezel sets for RetroArch-style presentation None ScreenScraper Per-ROM-hash metadata + media for emulated games (ROM hash matching) Required ( SCREENSCRAPER_USER / SCREENSCRAPER_PASSWORD plus SCREENSCRAPER_DEV_ID / SCREENSCRAPER_DEV_PASSWORD in ~/.env ) Plugin providers Metadata and media from an enabled plugin that declares the capability Per plugin; see its manifest and settings Since 1.18.0, optional provider tokens can also be saved inside the app under Settings → Metadata & Media → Integration tokens and are shown masked. They cover IGDB, ScreenScraper, SteamGridDB, Gameyfin, and RetroAchievements, and they are separate from the required environment credentials above: a stored token does not replace IGDB_CLIENT_ID / IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET , the ScreenScraper pair, or STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY . See [Per-provider integration tokens](/integrations/accounts-and-media/ per-provider-integration-tokens). Priority is configurable: metadata_provider_priority orders built-in and plugin metadata providers, and plugin results can be preferred for bulk media ( plugin_metadata_priority ). Every search result is labelled with its source. Media from these providers feeds the durable download queue, which survives a restart and supports pause, resume, cancel, retry, and per-item errors. title: Metadata and media
description: Match games and manage local artwork and media jobs.
body: Metadata sync uses the LaunchBox Games Database (LBGDB) when its local copy is available. The database downloads from https://gamesdb.launchbox-app.com/Metadata.zip and is built into a local SQLite file at /metadata/launchbox.db . The first download can be large (up to 2 GiB allowed); it runs as a background job visible through the operation's status endpoint. Download and search Open a game's detail pane and click Find metadata to open the LaunchBox Games Database dialog. Use Download database to fetch and build the local database (it skips when a download is already running and reports the job state). Then Search matches the game title (or your query) with the game's platform as a hint, returning up to 20 results ordered by exact normalized match, platform match, then shortest name. Without a database, the search route returns HTTP 409 with "Download the LaunchBox metadata database first." Select a result to apply fields: name, platform, year, developer, publisher, genre, description, series, ESRB, and max players. Check Box front , Background , and Screenshots to also download media (up to 12 screenshots); Replace existing fields and media (overwrite) updates values that are already set, otherwise only empty fields are filled. Downloads go to /media/launchbox/ / . ESRB values are accepted from the standard set (E, E10+, T, M, AO, RP, EC, K-A, Unrated). The game keeps a launchbox_db_id so later jobs can find it. Metadata Match Review After batch imports, OpenBox provides a dedicated Metadata Match Review queue: - Preview Matches : POST /api/v2/metadata/matches/preview queues a metadata match preview for a batch or game set; GET /api/v2/metadata/matches/preview?preview_id= retrieves the preview result with candidate scores and field previews. - Inspect Candidates : GET /api/v2/metadata/matches/items returns paginated candidate lists with confidence scores and field previews. - Apply or Decide : - POST /api/v2/metadata/matches/decisions : Submits per-item accept/reject decisions for matched candidates. - POST /api/v2/metadata/matches/apply : Confirms matched metadata and artwork for selected items or entire batches. Search IGDB is an alternative provider; it needs IGDB_CLIENT_ID and IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET in ~/.env (Twitch developer app credentials). IGDB results apply name, summary/description, year, and genre. Use Steam data fills name, developer, publisher, genre, year, and description from the Steam storefront API for entries with a Steam App ID, and downloads the library cover and header image. Metadata provider priority Metadata searches can mix the built-in providers and enabled plugin providers in a configured order. Settings → Metadata & Media exposes Metadata provider priority, one per line ( metadata_provider_priority ) and Prefer plugin metadata providers in bulk downloads ( plugin_metadata_priority , off by default). - Priority list. title: SteamGridDB artwork and launcher trophies
description: Configure optional SteamGridDB artwork and understand OpenBox's separate deterministic trophy case.
body: OpenBox includes an optional SteamGridDB artwork provider and a separate local OpenBox launcher trophy case . SteamGridDB improves art coverage; launcher trophies summarize what your local library and play history already prove. Neither feature requires an OpenBox account. SteamGridDB artwork 1. Put STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY (alias OPENBOX_STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY ) in an owner-only ~/.env file or another supported environment file. 2. Leave Enable SteamGridDB artwork provider on in Settings → Integrations, or turn it off when the provider should not be contacted. 3. In the metadata dialog, use Search SteamGridDB for one game or Fill missing art via SteamGridDB for a bulk job. 4. Review the selected result and media kinds before applying it. The provider can supply covers, backgrounds, clear logos, icons, and banners. SteamGridDB results carry the steamgriddb source label, participate in the configured metadata provider priority, and are a valid source for the durable media queue (pause, resume, cancel, retry, per-item errors). OpenBox sends HTTPS requests to SteamGridDB, keeps a local disk cache, rejects unsafe media URLs, and reports provider/rate-limit failures as integration errors. The API key is never returned in settings or diagnostics. An optional per-provider SteamGridDB integration token can also be stored from Settings under Integration tokens ; it is kept out of the public settings view and shown masked (see [Accounts and media](/integrations/accounts-and-media/ per-provider-integration-tokens)). Without a key, or after the provider is disabled/rejected for the session, the rest of the library and other providers continue to work. Useful routes are: - GET /api/v2/steamgrid/status — enabled/configured/provider and cache status; - GET /api/v2/steamgrid/search?q=TITLE&limit=12 — bounded autocomplete results; - POST /api/v2/steamgrid/test — test the configured key; - POST /api/v2/steamgrid/info with — normalized metadata/media for review; - POST /api/v2/steamgrid/apply — queue selected metadata/media for one stable game id; and - POST /api/v2/steamgrid/match — queue a bulk fill for explicit ids or games missing covers. Apply and bulk match return 202 with a job_id ; inspect it through [Background jobs](/reference/background-jobs/). The provider is optional, external, and subject to its own account terms and rate limits. OpenBox launcher trophies The local Trophy Case opens from the View Trophy Case button in the success toast that appears when a new launcher trophy is awarded. The toast expires after a few seconds, and there is no persistent Trophy Case item in the 1.18 Tools menu. Tools → RetroAchievements account opens the separate RetroAchievements account dialog, not this local case. The evaluator reads only the current library and recorded history. It stores earn timestamps so an award toast is shown once, but awards are never revoked when metadata or history later changes. Trophy Rule --- --- Century Club 100 hours of total playtime Collector

title: Creating an OpenBox Plugin
description: Build, sandbox, and distribute plugins using standard JSON lifecycle hooks and capability declarations.
body: OpenBox plugins extend launcher functionality through decoupled lifecycle hooks. Each hook invocation runs in its own subprocess, in a Bubblewrap sandbox ( bwrap ) when available. A .py entry is driven by plugin_runner_v2.py over a JSON Lines frame; a native executable entry receives the same JSON Lines request directly. Plugin Manifest ( plugin.json ) Every plugin requires a plugin.json manifest placed in its directory under ~/.local/share/openbox-game-launcher/plugins/ / : Manifest Fields Field Type Description --- --- --- id string Unique plugin identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-] $ (lowercase start, 2-64 characters). This is the install directory name. name string Display name shown in the Plugins dialog. version string Non-empty version string (e.g. 1.0.0 ). description string Optional short summary of plugin capabilities (500 characters). author string Optional author name (80 characters) shown with the plugin. homepage string Optional HTTPS project URL (300 characters). entry string Entry point inside the package (defaults to plugin.py ). A .py file runs through plugin_runner_v2.py ; any other executable file runs directly. It must resolve inside the package, with no symlinks or .. . hooks array Subscribed hooks: the six base hooks ( before_launch , after_session , library , command , library_source , events ) plus the six capability hooks ( storefront , metadata , media , stats , emulator , discovery ). api_version integer Required. Must be 2 in 3.0. A missing value or 1 fails with PLUGIN_API_RETIRED . Version 2 uses the JSON Lines runner and unlocks min_openbox , subscriptions , and the versioned read-only host services ( library.query , media.search ). min_openbox string v2 only: oldest OpenBox release that may serve the plugin; older hosts refuse it at load. subscriptions array v2 only: named events the runner delivers, on top of the base events hook. commands array Up to 32 entries, exposed in the command palette under the prefix. permissions array Declared permissions; the only permission is network , granted by the user in the Plugins manager. settings object JSON Schema subset for per-plugin settings; the Plugins manager and Settings Plugins render a form and inject stored values into hook payloads. capabilities object Capability declarations (1.18.0+). Each requires its matching hook and is what makes a plugin act like a built-in source. messages object Localized notification templates (1.18.0+), resolved against the active locale.
