title: Plugins guide
description: Install and use local plugins to extend OpenBoxGL.
body: Plugins are optional local packages that observe or extend OpenBoxGL through lifecycle hooks. A v2 plugin entry may be a Python file or a native executable; each invocation runs in its own process, so a plugin that crashes or misbehaves cannot take down the library. Plugin API v1 was removed in 3.0: every manifest must declare "api_version": 2 or it fails with PLUGIN_API_RETIRED . Without bubblewrap, isolation is robustness, not a security sandbox. The child process shares your user privileges and your filesystem, it can read and write any file your OpenBoxGL process can reach. The per-hook timeout (5 seconds for base hooks), the payload caps (2 MiB in; 4 MiB out for a api_version: 2 plugin), and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 environment cleaning prevent runaway behavior, but they don't restrict what the plugin can see on disk. When bwrap (bubblewrap) is available, OpenBoxGL runs plugins in an OS sandbox ( --unshare-all , --ro-bind / / , tmpfs on /home / /tmp / /run , no network); if the sandbox cannot be created, enabled plugins are skipped unless you trust the plugin in the Plugins manager ("Trust and run", bound to the package's SHA-256) or set OPENBOX_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_PLUGINS=1 for trusted local plugins. What a plugin can do Base hooks run on lifecycle events: Hook When it runs What it can change --- --- --- library On every library read Rewrites the games list shown in the UI. Python fallback only in 3.0 — the Rust server does not invoke it yet. before_launch At launch, after profile/archive resolution Rewrites the launch args / cwd , or cancels the launch with an error. Python fallback only in 3.0. after_session After a session ends Observes the session record; the result is discarded. Python fallback only in 3.0. command When a command-palette entry is picked (1.14.0+) Returns a notification to display; adds entries to the palette. library_source On every library read, if declared (1.14.0+) Contributes imported games to your library. Python fallback only in 3.0. events On lifecycle events (1.14.0+) Observes lifecycle events. The Rust server emits app_startup and app_shutdown ; the Python fallback also emits scan_finished , playtime_milestone , game_added , game_removed , and game_updated . Capability hooks (1.18.0) let a plugin act like a built-in source. title: RetroAchievements
description: Connect RetroAchievements, match ROMs to achievement sets, and track progress.
body: OpenBoxGL integrates with [RetroAchievements](https://retroachievements.org/) to match your ROMs to achievement sets, show earned and hardcore progress, serve badges, and inject your credentials into emulator configs so emulators enable achievements themselves. RetroAchievements matches games by content hash of the ROM or disc image, not by filename or size: MD5 for most cartridge and disc formats, Dolphin's SHA-1 for RVZ images, and the rcheevos TMD/content layout for WiiWare WADs. That's why two different dumps of "Super Mario Bros" (NES) can have different hashes, they're treated as separate games with separate achievement sets. If a ROM doesn't match any set, try a different dump from No-Intro, Redump, or a well-known source; header-stripping is applied automatically for NES, SNES, Atari 7800, Lynx, and PC Engine, and N64 byte order is normalised for .v64 and .n64 dumps. What it does - Matches ROMs to achievement sets by content hash. - Shows progress per game: earned, hardcore, beaten, mastered. - Serves achievement badges in the game detail pane. - Injects credentials into RetroArch, Dolphin, and PCSX2 configs so those emulators can enable achievements during play. Set it up 1. Get credentials. Create a RetroAchievements account and generate a web API key on your RetroAchievements profile page. 2. Enter them in Tools → RetroAchievements account (username + web API key), or set the environment variables in ~/.env : - RETROACHIEVEMENTS_USERNAME (aliases RA_USERNAME , OPENBOX_RA_USERNAME ) - RETROACHIEVEMENTS_API_KEY (aliases RA_API_KEY , RETROACHIEVEMENTS_KEY , OPENBOX_RA_API_KEY ) 3. Credentials are validated against API_GetUserProfile.php before saving and stored in retroachievements.json (mode 0o600 ). 4. Open a game's detail pane. If its platform supports auto-matching, use the RetroAchievements section to match the ROM. Matching RetroAchievements matching is by ROM hash, so the local file must be the exact ROM the achievement set expects. Hashing supports: Platform Notes --- --- NES, SNES Header stripping applied Nintendo 64 Byte-swapped .v64 / .n64 handled Game Boy / Color / Advance — Sega Genesis / Mega Drive — Master System, Game Gear — Atari 2600 Raw image hashed Atari 7800, Lynx Header stripping applied PC Engine Header stripping applied Arcade Matched by set name Wii / WiiWare .wad files are hashed with the rcheevos TMD/content layout RetroAchievements expects GameCube / Wii .rvz disc images are hashed through dolphin-tool PlayStation .chd images are hashed from their first data track through chdman Multi-disc sets A .m3u playlist resolves to its first existing disc image, relative to the playlist ROMs inside ZIP and 7z archives are hashed too (each archive's largest member is capped at 512 MiB, plain ROMs also capped at 512 MiB before hashing; larger files return 400 with ROM file is too large ). For other platforms, enter a RetroAchievements Game ID manually in Edit metadata . Disc and playlist formats - M3U : the first non-comme

title: Achievement Trail
description: Offline RetroAchievements analytics — velocity, ETAs, next-up queues, and milestones.
body: Achievement Trail (ADR 0110, 3.0) turns the local RetroAchievements cache into an offline analytics view. It never calls the RetroAchievements API to render the trail; it reads cache/retroachievements/ and keeps a derived cache/trail.json . What it shows - 8-week ISO velocity — unlock counts per ISO week, so a burst and a dry spell are visible side by side. - Completion ETA — a confidence-rated estimate based on your recent unlock rate. - Next 100-point milestone — the achievement points total and the gap to the next round number. - Cheapest-first next-up queue — remaining achievements ordered by points per unit of estimated effort. - Streaks — consecutive active weeks. Refresh The trail is stale-while-rebuild. When the cache changes, the UI keeps the previous trail and offers Refresh ; a refresh is a cancellable background job. GET /api/v2/ra/trail returns the current trail and GET /api/v2/ra/trail/game?game_id=… returns one game's detail. Cache behavior - cache/trail.json is keyed by a signature of the RetroAchievements cache. A signature change rebuilds it; more than 250 changed files trigger a background rebuild. - Older caches without date_earned or date_earned_hardcore degrade with an explicit notice instead of inventing dates. - The trail is local and offline. Deleting cache/trail.json loses only the derived view; it rebuilds from cache/retroachievements/ . Related pages - [RetroAchievements](/guides/retroachievements/) - [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/) - [Data and recovery](/reference/data-and-recovery/)

title: Activity Center & Durable Operations
description: Monitor running tasks, background operations, cancellations, and restart recovery.
body: OpenBox manages all background operations through the durable Operation Service ( crates/openbox-store/src/operations.rs ), backed by operations.json in your data directory. Features - Activity Drawer : Click the Activity button ( activityButton ) in the top bar to inspect running and historical operations. In 3.0 routine running-job badges are calm neutral pills (red is reserved for errors), filters are a 2-column row, internal job types are humanized, and redundant single-job "Grouped by run" duplicates are removed. - Real-Time Progress : Live Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream progress updates, byte counters, and status messages ( GET /api/v2/events ). - Cancellation & Safety : In-flight operations can be cancelled cleanly without leaving corrupted or half-written states ( POST /api/v2/jobs/cancel with job_id in the JSON body). - Restart Recovery : If OpenBox is closed or restarted while an operation is running, the task is marked interrupted . You can resume or retry it with one click. Supported Operations - Library Imports : Folder scanning, archive inspection, and storefront auto-imports ( storefront.auto_import ). - Metadata Synchronization : LaunchBox Games Database downloads and batch matching ( metadata.db_sync , metadata.match_preview , metadata.apply ). - Media Downloads : Artwork, screenshot, and video fetching ( media.bulk_download , media.cleanup , media.memories_import ). The media queue is durable: it survives restarts, supports pause, resume, cancel, retry, and per-item errors, and reports items , queue , and per-state counts . - Storefront scans and imports : Startup scans report per-source progress, skip sources with no library games, and stop after a 30-second budget while keeping partial results. - ScreenScraper and SteamGridDB : hash scraping and artwork jobs ( screenscraper.match , screenscraper.apply , steamgrid.match , steamgrid.apply ). - Library Export : JSON/CSV projections queued as durable jobs ( library.export ). - Clips and Reels : local reel creation ( clips.reel ). - Emulator Management : Flathub emulator installations and updates. - Backups : Library backup creation and save state archiving.

title: Sessions, saves, and backups
description: Track play and protect library and save data.
body: OpenBoxGL records session history, play counts, play time, last-played state, and exit outcomes when tracking is enabled, and protects both save data and the whole library with versioned backups. Every active session, queue entry, and save backup points at a game_id derived from the game's identity (path, platform, store ids), never its position in the list. Completed history records store the game title string, start timestamp, elapsed duration, and exit code. That is why reordering your library, re-importing, or deleting other games never breaks the link between a session and its game. See [How OpenBoxGL works](/reference/how-it-works/ the-state-store) for the identity model. Sessions and history Every launch starts a session: play count increments, last-played stamps, and the first-launch progress setting applies. When the session ends (see tracking modes in [Emulators and launching](/guides/emulators-and-launching/)), play time adds, the session history records game, start time, duration, and exit code (history keeps the last 2,000 entries), and progress automation may move the game to Playing or Paused. Track play session history in Settings disables history recording while still tracking current sessions. Back up saves when a game session ends is a 2.x behavior; the 3.0 Rust server does not currently call the session-end save/vault/OBS/stats hooks. Use the manual Save management actions until those hooks are wired. Active sessions are mirrored to sessions.json beside library.json (2.0) so a crash can reconcile them at startup; the file is removed when no sessions remain. The Running dialog (top bar) shows live sessions with Pause/Resume, Restart, Exit, and Force close. The History dialog lists past sessions with timestamps, durations, and exit codes. A session that fails fast (under 5 seconds, nonzero exit) shows a "Session failed" overlay with the code and a hint to check the Launch command and emulator install. Since 1.16.0 the long-run case is distinguished too: a game that ran for a while and then exited with an error shows Session ended with the exit code, rather than the ordinary "Play time and history were saved". A normal exit still shows the usual message. The same two values reach [webhooks](/integrations/webhooks/) — the exit code, plus a separate timed_out flag when a session ended because it timed out rather than failing. Save discovery Per game, Save management offers Discover locations , Back up now , Version history , a state slot, Ludusavi and Hoard actions, and Scan library for saves (in the Library checkup dialog) which applies discovered paths to every game at once. Discovery knows the common locations: - Steam Cloud : ~/.local/share/Steam/userdata/ / /remote (also .steam/steam and the Flatpak path). - PlayStation 2 : PCSX2 memcards (native and Flatpak). - PSP : PPSSPP PSP/SAVEDATA . - PlayStation 3 : RPCS3 dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata . - GameCube : Dolphin GC . - Wii / WiiWare : Dolphin Wii/title . - Sega Saturn : R

title: Library backups
description: Create, rotate, and restore whole-library backup archives.
body: The Backup dialog (Tools → Backup) creates whole-library ZIP archives under /backups/ named OpenBoxBackup-%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S-%f.zip . Each archive contains a manifest plus any of: settings, library, media, plugins, themes, and extension data. The Gameyfin password, the OBS WebSocket password, the per-provider integration tokens (IGDB, ScreenScraper, SteamGridDB, Gameyfin, RetroAchievements), and webhook secrets are redacted from export and safely preserved on restore. Create a backup 1. Open Tools → Backup . 2. Click Create backup . The dialog has no item picker and no rotation control: every archive holds the library, settings, media, plugins, and themes, and the newest 7 archives are kept. 3. Backup and restore are refused while any game is running. extension_data can only be selected through the API or the CLI ( --backup --items ...,extension_data ). When items is omitted, the API and the CLI default to library + settings; the API's keep default is 0 (no rotation), while Create backup uses 7. The CLI form is: The archive is written via a temp file and os.replace , then the directory is fsynced. If you include plugins , the archive stores the installed packages and the plugin state file but not the capability credential store, and password-format plugin settings are blanked. Local password values are merged back when that archive is restored, so a backup cannot leak a plugin secret or erase one on restore. The other redacted values — the Gameyfin and OBS WebSocket passwords, the per-provider integration tokens, and webhook secrets — are handled the same way: stripped from the archive, merged back from your local copy on restore. Scheduled automatic backups (v1.12.0) Settings can run the same engine on a weekly schedule: enable automatic backups , pick a retention of 1-52 archives (default 4), and an hourly daemon tick fires auto_backup_due() once seven days have passed since last_auto_backup — a missing or unparsable stamp counts as due. The automatic backup covers the library, settings, media, plugins, and themes — never extension data. Automatic archives are byte-identical to a manual backup in the default format 2, so the restore path below applies unchanged. Backup format 2 (2.0) 2.1 and 3.0 write backups in format 2 only . Format 2 records a SHA-256 hash for every archive member, and restore validates every member's hash and refuses a corrupt member or a member the manifest does not list ( BACKUP_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED on an archive format this build cannot read) before writing anything. Format 1 archives still restore, but a new format 1 write returns 410 BACKUP_FORMAT_RETIRED ; use a 2.0.x build if you need a 1.19-compatible export. Save Vault snapshots are not in BACKUP_ITEMS ; copy /save-vault/ separately. Restore a backup Restore is guarded at every step: 1. Refused while any game is running. 2. The data directory must not be a symlink. 3. Every member is validated before any write: no empty names, NUL bytes, absolute paths, .. , duplicate

title: Library catalog sync
description: Sync game catalog metadata across machines through a mounted folder with preview, conflict review, and recovery.
body: OpenBoxGL can synchronize your game catalog — names, platforms, metadata, store IDs, tags — between machines through any mounted folder (Syncthing, Dropbox, Nextcloud, a network share, or a plain local path). This is the opt-in v3 sync added in 1.10.0, separate from [statistics sync](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/statistics-sync/), which only merges play data. Only an explicit allowlist of catalog fields travels: the stable game_id , names, sort titles, alternate names, platform, genre, year, developer, publisher, series, region, ESRB, max players, description, notes, Wikipedia URL, source , store/provider IDs (Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Gameyfin, IGDB, RetroAchievements, LaunchBox), disc count, ROM name, clone_of , set type, manual-entry flag, tags, and the sync identity field ( library_sync_id ). File paths, launch commands, install configuration, credentials, play statistics, unknown custom fields, and user metadata always stay local. Syncing a catalog does not copy games, ROMs, saves, or media — a game that arrives from another machine needs its own local launch setup. GOG, EA, and Ubisoft provider IDs, price paid, currency, and Game Night decks are not in the allowlist and stay local. A mixed-version peer would reject an event carrying fields it does not know, so those values are deliberately kept out of the protocol rather than risking the whole event. Set it up 1. In Settings → Integrations , set the mounted cloud folder to the absolute path of a folder that is mounted and writable on every participating machine. 2. Check Enable opt-in library catalog sync . The setting refuses to save without a folder. 3. Repeat on each machine that should share the catalog. Each device generates its own persistent device ID on first use. Sync is fully manual and explicit — there is no background scheduling. The workflow is: publish your changes, let the folder replicate, then preview and apply on the other machine. The preview → review → apply workflow The Library catalog sync card in Settings has three buttons: - Preview catalog changes ( POST /api/v2/library/sync/preview ) reads the remote event objects in the folder and shows what would change: additions · updates · deletions · conflicts , plus a per-game change list. Preview is read-only — it writes nothing. - Apply reviewed changes stays disabled until a preview succeeds and every conflict has a chosen value. Applying first writes a private recovery snapshot of your library, then commits against current state in one transaction. - Publish local changes ( POST /api/v2/library/sync/publish ) writes your local catalog edits as new event objects so other machines can see them. If the library or the remote folder changes between preview and apply, the preview is rejected as stale — run preview again to rebind it to the current state. Apply cannot run on a stale plan. title: Quick Resume, Moments, and Record That
description: Resume supported emulator sessions, capture play moments, and save local clips and reels.
body: OpenBox 1.11 keeps the context around a session close to the game. Quick Resume restores a stored emulator state where the selected adapter supports it; Moments bookmark a point in a session; and Record That saves a replay-buffer clip or a screenshot fallback. Quick Resume Quick Resume is capability-aware. When a launch adapter has a state definition, OpenBox can capture a state at the end of a session and show a Resume action in the game detail surface. The state is stored locally under the data directory and is fingerprinted with the adapter/emulator information that produced it. Current state-capable adapter families include Dolphin, DuckStation, MAME, PCSX2, PPSSPP, RetroArch, RPCS3, and ScummVM. Cemu, Eden, melonDS, Vita3K, xemu, and Xenia currently declare state: none ; they can still use Moments screenshots and notes, but they do not expose a Quick Resume state. Custom per-game commands and profiles may also be unable to resume even when a related emulator has a state-capable definition. To use it: 1. Leave Quick Resume enabled in Settings → Sessions & Saves. 2. Launch a game through its normal OpenBox profile and end the session normally when possible. 3. Use Resume from the game detail pane or call POST /api/v2/resume with the stable game id. 4. If the emulator or adapter changed, the state is marked stale. Start clean, or make an explicit decision to allow the stale state through the API; do not treat a stale state as guaranteed compatible. state_retention controls how many archived state files are retained (1–20). Starting a game clean does not silently delete the stored resume state; use Discard resume state or POST /api/v2/resume/discard when you want to remove it. Per-game state slot The game's Save management card stores an optional State slot ( resume_slot ). Enter 1–32 letters, digits, - , or _ ; the value is saved through POST /api/v2/resume/slot and used wherever the selected adapter's state template names a slot, both when OpenBox arms capture and when it reloads the state. Leaving the field blank uses the default names ( openbox-session for capture, openbox-resume for reload, which is what MAME expects). An invalid value is rejected with RESUME_SLOT_INVALID and the field reverts to the stored value, so a typo cannot silently change which slot an emulator writes. Moments Press M in the desktop library, use the capture action in the pause/recap surface, or create a Moment from the API. A Moment can contain: - a title, note, trigger, timestamp, and launch id; - a screenshot captured by the first available local screenshot tool, or a supplied approved media path; and - an immutable resume snapshot only when Quick Resume is enabled, available, non-stale, and supported by the adapter. Automatic Moments (first boot, RetroAchievements unlock, progress, and milestones) are controlled by Moments autocapture ( moments_autocapture , default on): when it is off, automatic triggers are skipped while manual captures still work ( crates/open

title: Save Vault
description: Indexed, SHA-256-verified save snapshots with manual, on-close, and scheduled triggers.
body: Save Vault (ADR 0109, 3.0) keeps indexed snapshots of a game's saves under /save-vault/ . It is separate from the per-game save backups and the whole-library backup: vault snapshots are fast to list, verify, diff, and restore, and they are not included in BACKUP_ITEMS . Enable and configure Open Settings Sessions Save Vault , or set the four keys directly: Setting Default Meaning --- --- --- save_vault_enabled true Enables the vault. session_close and auto snapshots require it. save_vault_keep 5 Snapshots kept per game, 1-50. Older snapshots are pruned. pre-restore safety snapshots are exempt. save_vault_on_close false Takes a session_close snapshot when a game session ends. save_vault_auto_days 0 Days between automatic auto snapshots, 0-365. 0 disables the schedule. 3.0 scheduling note: the Rust server's hourly tick currently unlocks time capsules and refreshes tray recents; it does not call auto_vault_due . Manual and on-close snapshots work, but the scheduled auto pass does not fire under openbox-server yet. Use the manual Create snapshot action until the scheduler is wired. Take a snapshot Open the game's Save management card and choose Save Vault Create snapshot , or call: Triggers are manual , session_close , auto , and pre-restore . A pre-restore snapshot is taken automatically before every restore and is never pruned. Inspect and restore The tabbed Save History dialog lists snapshots newest first with size, trigger, and file count. Select one to see a diff of added, changed, and unchanged files. Restore always takes the pre-restore safety snapshot first. It validates the snapshot manifest and refuses symlinked destinations or paths outside the game's save roots. Limits and storage - A snapshot is capped at 512 MiB and 5,000 files . - Vault use above 5 GiB shows a disk warning; lower retention or delete old snapshots. - Shared emulator roots are excluded automatically so the vault does not duplicate every game's memory card or state directory. - index.json is self-healing: a malformed or missing index is rebuilt from the snapshot directories on load. - Vault snapshots live outside BACKUP_ITEMS . To copy the vault off-machine, copy /save-vault/ alongside your ZIP backups. Related pages - [Save discovery and restore](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/saves/) - [Library backups](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/library-backups/) - [Save Vault API](/reference/api/saves-and-operations/ save-vault)

title: Save discovery and restore
description: Discover save locations, inspect backup versions, and restore only the files you choose.
body: OpenBoxGL can discover where a game keeps its saves, back them up into versioned archives, and restore them with hard safety checks. Since 1.18.0 each backup also describes every archived file, so you can see what a restore would change and restore only the files you check. Before you start - The game must have a local file ( path ) so OpenBoxGL can identify it. - Save management is enabled by default. Enable save management and backups in Settings can hide the card and refuse save routes ( "Save management is disabled." ). - Saving works per game from the Save management card in the detail pane, or library-wide from the Library checkup dialog ( Scan library for saves ). - Optional tools on PATH : [Ludusavi](https://github.com/mtkennerly/ludusavi) and [Hoard](https://github.com/rleeon/hoard) add external save-tool actions. Discover save locations Open a game's Save management and choose Discover locations . OpenBoxGL looks in the common places for each platform: Platform Location checked --- --- Steam Cloud ~/.local/share/Steam/userdata/ / /remote (also .steam/steam and the Flatpak path) PlayStation 2 PCSX2 memcards (native and Flatpak) PSP PPSSPP PSP/SAVEDATA PlayStation 3 RPCS3 dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata GameCube Dolphin GC Wii / WiiWare Dolphin Wii/title Wii U Cemu mlc01/usr/save Sega Saturn RetroArch saves (or ~/.mednafen ) RetroArch any save or state file under saves / states whose stem matches the game name macOS Steam Cloud under ~/Library/Application Support/Steam ; PPSSPP ~/.config/ppsspp/PSP/SAVEDATA ; RPCS3 and Dolphin under ~/Library/Application Support ; RetroArch ~/Documents/RetroArch saves and states. See [macOS](/macos/ saves-on-macos). Candidates are shown as path + label + shared . Confirm them per game, or run Scan library for saves to apply discovered paths to every game at once. Confirmed paths are stored on the game ( save_paths ) and drive the library's Has saves view. Store a state slot The same card has a State slot field for RetroArch save states. Enter 1–32 letters, digits, - , or _ and press Enter; the value is stored on the game ( resume_slot ) and used when Quick Resume captures and reloads that game's state. Leaving it blank restores the default slot. The route behind the field is POST /api/v2/resume/slot with ; an invalid slot returns RESUME_SLOT_INVALID with "Resume slot must be 1-32 letters, digits, '-' or '_'." See [Quick Resume and Moments](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/quick-resume-moments/) for what uses the slot. Back up saves Back up now creates a ZIP per game under /save-backups/ / named YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS- .zip containing a manifest.json and the configured save roots. Details: - Every file is described before archiving with its size, permission mode, modification time, and SHA-256, so later previews and restores can compare content rather than timestamps. - Files are backed up individually; directories are walked. Files are opened without following symlinks. - Symlinks in save paths or in the backu

title: Statistics sync
description: Merge play statistics across machines through a mounted cloud folder.
body: OpenBoxGL merges play statistics between machines through any mounted folder, Syncthing, Dropbox, Nextcloud, Drive, or a plain local path. The folder must be mounted and writable on every machine that should participate. Set it up 1. In Settings → Integrations , set Mounted cloud folder to the absolute path of the mounted folder (for example /mnt/cloud/openbox ). 2. Click Sync statistics now to run a merge immediately. The Python fallback also runs a merge after each session; the 3.0 Rust server does not currently call that hook, so use the button until it is wired. 3. Configure the same folder on another machine to merge stats there. What syncs and how conflicts resolve Sync reads and writes openbox-statistics.json (format 1) in the folder under a file lock. Per game: Field Merge rule --- --- play_count , playtime_seconds By maximum last_played Newer timestamp wins progress , rating , favorite Whoever played last is authoritative; if neither side has played, the newer file wins generated_at Preserved when the remote was newer, bumped when local state is newer Deleted local games are never resurrected : games present only in the cloud file are dropped from the merged output, and only games that exist locally are written back. This keeps a removal on one machine from reappearing on another. Troubleshooting Problem Cause / fix --- --- "Configure a mounted cloud sync folder first." No cloud_folder set in Settings; point it at a mounted, writable path. Sync does nothing after a session Check the folder is mounted and the file is writable; look for sync errors in the diagnostic log. Stats reappear after deleting a game Deletion does not remove the cloud file's entry for that game. Run a sync after deletion so the merged output drops it. Catalog sync Statistics sync above covers play stats only. Catalog metadata travels through a separate opt-in transport: turn on Enable opt-in library catalog sync under Settings → Integrations after setting the mounted folder, then use Preview catalog changes ( POST /api/v2/library/sync/preview ), Apply reviewed changes ( POST /api/v2/library/sync/apply ), and Publish local changes ( POST /api/v2/library/sync/publish ). Launch paths, commands, credentials, play statistics, installed files, saves, and media stay on each device; the legacy whole-library publish/pull routes return 503 LIBRARY_SYNC_UNAVAILABLE . See [Library catalog sync](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/library-sync/) for the workflow, conflict review, and the exact field allowlist. See also - [Library catalog sync](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/library-sync/), opt-in catalog metadata sync (v1.10.0) - [Sessions, saves, and backups](/guides/sessions-saves-and-backups/), session recording and history - [API saves and operations](/reference/api/saves-and-operations/), POST /api/v2/cloud/sync - [Data and recovery](/reference/data-and-recovery/), where local state lives

title: Storefront Manager
description: Browse owned and installed catalogs, import either set, and automate imports.
body: The Storefront Manager dialog (Tools → Game stores) browses your storefront catalogs, owned versus installed, and imports either set into the library. Steam and Gameyfin are available on every platform, Heroic on Linux and Windows, and Lutris on Linux only. Native GOG Galaxy, EA app, and Ubisoft Connect installs are imported on Windows. OpenBoxGL distinguishes between what you own on a storefront and what you actually have installed on disk. Importing "installed" gives you games ready to play; importing "owned / uninstalled" gives you placeholders so your catalog reflects your entire library ahead of time. The Play button on an uninstalled entry stays greyed-out (or becomes INSTALL for Gameyfin, and for a Steam game whose install folder is missing) until the game's local files appear. This separation lets you see your full collection without needing every title downloaded simultaneously. Scanning storefronts Scan storefronts ( POST /api/v2/storefront/scan ) refreshes installed state without deleting games. Each source is scanned in its own child process with a 30-second budget ( STOREFRONT_SCAN_TIMEOUT ); a source that exceeds it is recorded as timeout and the scan moves on rather than hanging on one launcher. The dialog shows a row per source with its live status — pending , running , ok , skipped , timeout , or error — the games it resolved, and its last scan time, so progress is visible per source rather than as one spinner. A source with no storefront installed and no games already in the library is skipped instead of probed. The scan writes its per-source status to storefront-status.json in the data directory, and GET /api/v2/storefront/status returns the same list the dialog renders. A scan that runs into the budget stops there and keeps what it already found: a source that times out or errors leaves the library untouched, so the sources scanned before it stay applied — the saved state stays valid and the next scan picks up where this one stopped. What each source shows Source Owned list comes from Installed list comes from --- --- --- Steam userdata/ /config/localconfig.vdf steamapps/appmanifest_ .acf Heroic (Linux and Windows) store_cache library JSON installed manifests ( legendaryConfig , gog_store , nile_config ) Epic legendaryConfig/legendary/installed.json , or ~/.config/legendary/installed.json the same manifests Lutris (Linux only) lutris --list-games --json lutris --list-games --installed --json Gameyfin The configured server's catalog The same catalog, filtered to installed titles GOG Galaxy (Windows) Not imported Registry entries plus each game's goggame- .info EA app (Windows) Not imported EA installerdata.xml manifests Ubisoft Connect (Windows) Not imported Ubisoft Installs registry keys Import Epic ( POST /api/v2/import/epic ) reads Epic on its own through Legendary, and also reads Epic Games Launcher Windows manifests when they are present. It is a source in its own right rather than part of Heroic: use it when you keep Epic

title: Creating Custom Themes
description: Author custom CSS themes using OpenBox's design system tokens.
body: OpenBox features a strict, token-driven CSS architecture. Every color, surface, font, and border is driven by standard CSS variables defined in :root . Design System Tokens When creating a custom theme, you only need to override :root variables. No component CSS rules are modified. The table below is the minimal starter subset for the default palette: warm near-black surfaces, off-white text, a teal focus signal, a brand-orange selection/action ramp, and a matching action-ink. The full contract is much larger — mood-match ( --mood- ), constellation edge ( --constellation-edge- ), mastery ( --mastery- ), overlay-insight, gamepad, health, toast, and font tokens — and is documented on the [Design system](/project/design-system/) page. Start with these, then override more as needed. The Themes dialog renders every theme, including Default, as a card with five swatches sampled from --bg , --surface-card , --brand , --text , and --muted , so define all five for a representative preview. The gallery reads the values from your CSS file; it does not execute the stylesheet. Text and interactive colors should use the semantic ink tokens rather than raw palette entries: --ink-strong for primary headings, --on-active for text on an active tab or selection, --on-danger for text on a danger surface, --border-input for form borders, and --state-hover / --state-press for interaction states. The hover and press tokens are alpha overlays rather than foregrounds and are deliberately not part of the matrix. The duration and easing tokens ( --dur-fast , --dur-base , --dur-slow , --dur-out , --dur-spin , --dur-loop , --stagger , and the --ease- family) are structural, not themable . The reduced-motion block targets :root:root , so it outranks a theme's :root regardless of load order; redeclaring the tokens in a theme does not change motion, it only splits the contract in two. title: Troubleshooting backups and restores
description: Diagnose refused backups, stale restores, and failed restores.
body: Both whole-library backups and per-game save backups validate hard before writing. Most problems are a specific refusal message; start with that message and the diagnostic log. Backup refused Message Cause / fix --- --- "Close running games before creating a backup." A game session is active; close games first (Running dialog). Applies to create and restore. "Backup source is a symlink: ..." Backup refuses symlinks anywhere in the source tree. Point the item at real files. "Save management is disabled." The save-management toggle is off. Enable it under Settings Sessions & Saves (save management and backups); the read routes return instead of failing while it is off. Restore refused Message Cause / fix --- --- BACKUP_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED The archive declares a format this build cannot read (2.0 writes format 2; 1.19.x reads format 1). Use a 1.19-compatible export for older installs, or upgrade the restore side. Manifest hash mismatch or unlisted member Format 2 records a SHA-256 per member and refuses a corrupt or unlisted file before writing anything — restore a different archive or re-export. "This backup is older than the current library. Pass force=True to restore it anyway." The archive predates the current library. Only force when you intentionally want the older state; the current library is saved to library.before-restore.json first. "Backup archive is invalid." / "Backup manifest is invalid." Not a ZIP or missing manifest. Only OpenBoxBackup- .zip archives inside the data directory or backups/ are accepted. "Save backup roots do not match this game." The game's save_paths changed after the backup. Restore the archived paths (or back up again). "Save backup not found." The archive name is not inside the game's backup directory; use a name from the backup list. "Save backup manifest is invalid." / "Save backup manifest is too large." The archive's manifest.json is corrupt or over 1 MiB. Restore a different backup; the manifest is what maps archive members to save paths. "Select at least one save file to restore." selected was empty or not a list. Omit selected to restore the whole archive, or check at least one file. "Save selection does not match the backup." A selected archive path is not in this backup. Use names from the preview/manifest response. Restore fails on a symlink Restore rejects symlinks anywhere in the archive or destination tree (checked before and after each mkdir ). The preview buckets are add (absent on disk), overwrite (present with a different SHA-256), unchanged (same SHA-256), and missing (in the manifest but no longer in the archive). remove is always empty because a restore never deletes local files. title: Troubleshooting diagnostic logs
description: Read, copy, and share the rotating diagnostic log safely.
body: The diagnostic log is the first place to look when anything misbehaves. It records server activity, import/launch/session errors, job failures, and provider errors with credentials redacted. Where it lives - Path: /openbox.log (default ~/.local/share/openbox-game-launcher/openbox.log on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA%\openbox-game-launcher\openbox.log on Windows, and ~/Library/Application Support/openbox-game-launcher/openbox.log on macOS). - Rotation: 2 MiB per file, 4 rotations ( openbox.log.1 ... .4 ). - Redaction: tokens, passwords, secrets, API keys, and authorization values are redacted before writing. - It can still contain game names and local file paths , review it before sharing. Copy it Settings Advanced Copy diagnostic log copies a redacted diagnostic summary to the clipboard (it excludes secrets and the full log). This is the canonical way to attach diagnostics to an issue. The complete rotating log is available separately: GET /api/v2/log returns its last 64 KiB for local scripting, and GET /api/v2/diagnostic returns the same summary preview the button copies. How to use it 1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest local example (for example a single test ROM in a scratch folder). 2. Capture the exact visible error and the log section around it. Look for: - Import errors: which source, which manifest, what failed, and Storefront scan timed out after 30s. for a store that exceeded its budget. - Launch failures: the validation error or the session's exit code, and emulator-setting warnings ( RetroArch settings could not be written , Plugin emulator settings ). - Job failures: the job name and attempt ( openbox-job- workers), including media queue items whose last_error names the provider failure. - Provider errors: IGDB/EmuMovies/Gameyfin messages (secrets redacted), and The remote server returned an unsupported content type for a bad download. - apply_perf warnings when a TDP limit was expected but not applied. - Startup errors: a library that failed to load or was restored from the last-known-good backup. 3. Report with both the visible error and the copied log at [OpenBoxGL issues](https://github.com/vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL/issues). Security and credential problems belong in the [Security and legal](/policies/security/) policy. Related diagnostic files - /cache/launch_audit.json is the cached Launch Audit report read by the grid badges. The Python fallback also writes a rolling launch_audit.jsonl history (rotates to .1 at 5 MiB); the Rust server does not. - /media-queue.json is the durable media queue; failed items carry last_error and attempts. - /storefront-status.json (or the status file reported by GET /api/v2/storefront/status ) holds the last per-source scan state. These are caches, not library state; removing them loses history, not games. title: Troubleshooting imports
description: Diagnose Steam, Heroic, Lutris, arcade, Gameyfin, and folder import failures.
body: Start with the exact visible error and the diagnostic log ( Settings Advanced Copy diagnostic log ). Missing tools and malformed manifests are reported as import errors rather than silently creating unusable entries. Steam Check that one of ~/.local/share/Steam , ~/.steam/steam , or the Flatpak path contains steamapps/ with appmanifest_ .acf files (on macOS, ~/Library/Application Support/Steam ). Launching requires steam , the Steam Flatpak, or xdg-open on PATH ; otherwise the importer raises: POST /api/v2/import/steam returns : unreadable libraries are reported, not skipped silently. Each errors entry names the path and the OS error ( " : " ). A library on a read-only mount shows up here (for example " : Read-only file system" ) instead of importing zero games with no explanation. POST /api/v2/import/watch reports per-folder errors the same way. Imported Steam games record whether their install folder still exists. In the library, a missing install shows a red Missing badge and the play button becomes Install , which hands the game to Steam to install. An installed game offers Verify Steam files , which opens steam://validate/ so Steam performs verification and repair; OpenBox does not hash or replace the files. Neither action rewrites the imported record, so the badge clears on the next storefront scan once the install folder exists. Non-UTF8 file names survive the scan: folder scanners and Steam shortcut parsing decode with surrogateescape , so a foreign byte sequence never crashes the import — the entry imports under its surrogate-escaped name. Storefront scans and auto-import - POST /api/v2/storefront/scan queues a background scan ( 202 with job_id and sources ). GET /api/v2/storefront/status reports one entry per source with status , installed , last_scan , error , and games . - Each source gets a 30-second budget in its own child process. A timeout is recorded as and leaves that source untouched; sources already scanned stay applied and later sources still run. Re-run the scan after the store responds. - Sources with no install and no games already in the library are marked skipped instead of failing. - Per-source auto-import stores . enabled keeps importing that store, platform sets the target platform for its games, and include_uninstalled imports owned-but-uninstalled titles. A storefront import can also be limited to games that are not already in the library with only_new . - A legacy boolean storefront_auto_import entry is migrated to the object shape on the next settings save; until then readers accept both, so an enabled store keeps importing after the upgrade. - The watched-folder worker ticks every 10 seconds. A tick that finds nothing — an idle install, or a library that cannot be read — doubles the wait, up to 5 minutes, and the next tick that imports something returns it to 10 seconds. Heroic Manifests live under ~/.config/heroic ( legendaryConfig , gog_store , nile_config ) or the Flatpak path, plus standalone ~/.config/legend

title: Troubleshooting integration credentials
description: Diagnose RetroAchievements, IGDB, EmuMovies, and webhook credential problems.
body: Credentials are optional, and where each one comes from depends on the provider rather than on one global order. All credential values are redacted from the diagnostic log and never returned by the API ( _set booleans instead). - RetroAchievements — the saved retroachievements.json wins; the environment fills in what the file does not have. - EmuMovies — the saved emumovies.json wins; the environment fills in what the file does not have. - Steam — a saved value wins per field; the environment fills the gaps. - IGDB, ScreenScraper, SteamGridDB — environment only; the ~/.env pair or key is the only source. - Gameyfin — settings only; the URL, username, and password come from the settings dialog. In every case the process environment beats .env , because .env never overrides an existing variable. RetroAchievements - Required : username and web API key, from Settings RetroAchievements or ~/.env ( RETROACHIEVEMENTS_USERNAME / RETROACHIEVEMENTS_API_KEY , with aliases RA_USERNAME / RA_API_KEY and others). - Credentials are validated against API_GetUserProfile.php before saving; rejected credentials raise 400 "RetroAchievements rejected those credentials." (HTTP 401 / 403 or a profile without a User ). - Matching needs a local ROM file (ZIP and 7z hashing supported), and only supported platforms auto-match (NES, SNES, N64, GB/C/A, Genesis/MD, SMS, Game Gear, Atari 2600/7800, Lynx, PC Engine, Arcade by set name). Other platforms require entering a RetroAchievements Game ID manually in Edit metadata. - "Configure RetroAchievements first." means no credentials are saved. title: Troubleshooting launching
description: Diagnose launch validation errors, failed sessions, and archive extraction.
body: Launch failures fall into two groups: validation errors that stop the launch before any process starts, and sessions that start but fail. Start with the exact message in the game detail pane, then the diagnostic log. Validation errors (nothing starts) Message Cause / fix --- --- " has no launch path." The game has no path . Edit the game and set the game file path. "The configured path no longer exists: " The file was moved or deleted. Point the game at the new path under Edit game, or re-import the folder. " has no launch command and its file is not executable." Make the file executable ( chmod +x ), set a platform profile in Emulators & controllers , or set a per-game launch command in Edit metadata. "7z or 7zz is required to extract this archive." Non-ZIP archive extraction needs 7z or 7zz on PATH . ZIP is handled internally. "Launch canceled by a plugin." (or a plugin's error) A before_launch plugin canceled the launch. Check the plugin, or run with OPENBOX_SAFE_MODE=1 to bypass plugins. A game with no launch command and a non-executable file fails before any process starts with a message naming the game; set a platform profile or a per-game launch command. Session failed (exit code N) The process started and exited. Check: - The command tokens ( , , , ...), a wrong token substitutes an empty string, not an error. - The emulator binary and its install state/mode (native vs Flatpak) in Emulators & controllers . - Any BIOS files the game needs: use Emulators & controllers dependency check (DuckStation scph1001.bin , PCSX2 BIOS, RPCS3 firmware, RetroArch system directory). - Paths with spaces stay one argument because commands are tokenized, not shell-interpolated. If the emulator needs its own quoting, add quotes around in the profile. A failed extraction raises before any process starts. TDP / performance TDP limits (ryzenadj) never block a launch; check the log for apply_perf warnings if you expected a limit to apply. auto mode applies only on gamescope guests or battery-powered hosts. Display, fullscreen, effects, run-ahead, rewind, and upscaling are written to /emulator-configs/retroarch/ .cfg and attached as --appendconfig . If an existing --appendconfig is present, the generated path is appended after a comma instead of replacing it. description: Diagnose metadata database, media download, bezel, and duplicate cleanup problems.
body: Metadata and media work against local files and optional external providers. Start with the exact status/error and the diagnostic log. Metadata database - /api/v2/metadata/search and bulk media return 409 with "Download the LaunchBox metadata database first." until the database is downloaded (Artwork & details dialog, Download database ). - The first download can be large (up to 2 GiB allowed) and runs as a background job; poll the status endpoint until it reaches done . - An unreachable database fails the sync job with "Could not reach the metadata database ( ). Check the connection and try again." ( URLError / TimeoutError during LBDB sync no longer leak raw socket messages into the job panel). - A missing database returns 409 from readiness-dependent routes. Media downloads - Every download validates HTTP status, content type, and payload before it is written. A wrong type fails with "The remote server returned an unsupported content type: " ; an HTTP error fails with "The remote server returned HTTP ." ; an oversized response fails with "The download is too large." No partial file replaces a good one. - Per-kind limits: images 64 MiB ( image/ ), video 512 MiB ( video/ ), music 32 MiB ( audio/ or application/ogg ), manuals 64 MiB ( application/pdf ). LaunchBox Games Database images keep a 32 MiB cap (15 seconds for Steam covers). - Steam trailer/GOG media: responses read up to 4 MiB for JSON, downloads capped at 512 MiB. - EmuMovies requires a licensed account and correct credentials; the service rejects unlicensed credentials. - IGDB needs IGDB_CLIENT_ID and IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET in ~/.env ; missing credentials return 400 with the exact requirement. - Check credentials and rate limits first; provider failures are logged with secrets redacted. title: Troubleshooting plugins
description: Diagnose plugin launch failures, crashes, and safe mode.
body: Plugins are trusted local Python code that runs with your user privileges. When a plugin causes launch or library failures, the first tool is safe mode. Safe mode OPENBOX_SAFE_MODE=1 in the process environment disables plugin execution process-wide: library hooks, before_launch , after_session , and the webhook dispatcher all skip. The UI reports settings.safe_mode . It is the first thing to try when a plugin causes launch or library failures. Common failures Problem Cause / fix --- --- "Launch canceled by a plugin." / plugin error text A before_launch plugin returned . Remove or fix the plugin, or use safe mode. "A plugin returned an invalid launch command." / "...invalid working directory." A plugin returned structurally wrong output (empty argv, missing cwd , nonexistent working directory). Valid JSON that is wrong aborts the launch because launching with a broken command is worse. Plugin crashes/timeouts A crashing plugin can never break the app: the child process exits nonzero, times out, or returns invalid JSON, and its result is skipped with a warning. Only before_launch structural errors abort. "Plugin does not declare the hook." The installed manifest does not list that hook. Reinstall a package that declares it; a hook cannot be called just because the plugin is installed. "Plugin does not declare the capability." A storefront, metadata, media, stats, emulator-settings, or discovery entry was requested from a plugin whose manifest lacks that capability. "Grant network access to this plugin first." A plugin source needs the network permission. Grant it in the plugin's permissions dialog; grants can never exceed what the manifest declares. "Plugin does not declare permissions: ." The permission grant includes something outside the manifest's declared set. Update the plugin or narrow the grant. Plugin settings are missing from Settings Plugins Settings only render for enabled plugins with a valid settings schema. A disabled plugin's palette commands and settings forms do not load. "Plugin package needs a valid plugin.json." / "Plugin id, name, and version are required." The installed package is not a valid plugin. Install a package with a manifest ( id , name , version ; entry defaults to plugin.py ). A plugin update broke it Updates are atomic with rollback: the old version moves to plugins/.backups/ - during the swap and is restored on any failure. A local package changed on disk The recorded checksum no longer matches. POST /api/v2/plugins/repair reinstalls from the recorded package or the catalog; if the recorded file changed, reinstall it manually. Hook timeouts Legacy hooks keep a 5-second budget. Capability hooks get longer: storefront 30 s, metadata/media/stats 15 s, emulator/discovery 10 s. A hook that exceeds its budget is skipped with a warning; the library and launch still proceed. title: Troubleshooting state recovery
description: Diagnose corrupt library state and recover from the backup copy.
body: OpenBoxGL writes library state atomically with a last-known-good backup, so a crash or bad edit cannot silently corrupt the library. When corruption does happen, recovery is explicit and safe. How to read the state - The library is library.json (schema version 7) with a .bak last-known-good copy, a .lock file, and sessions.json for active sessions beside it. Writes are atomic and owner-only. - Stable game IDs ( game- ) survive reordering; legacy index-suffixed IDs are kept as aliases ( legacy_game_ids ). When recovery is needed If the primary file cannot be read, API operations return 503 with: The original file is preserved, never overwritten. Recover Recovery ( POST /api/v2/state/recover ) can inspect available backups or restore either the .bak file or a rolling snapshot: Dry-run inspection Send POST /api/v2/state/recover with to inspect recovery options without modifying state: Snapshot names embed the UTC timestamp to microseconds, a sequence number, and a random suffix ( - - .json ). Listing is newest-first by that embedded timestamp and sequence, not by file mtime, so two snapshots written in the same clock tick still sort correctly. A hand-placed filename without that format falls back to mtime ordering. Restoring state - Restore last-known-good backup : POST /api/v2/state/recover with loads library.json.bak , validates/normalizes it, and commits it atomically. - Restore specific snapshot : POST /api/v2/state/recover with restores a point-in-time snapshot from library.json.snapshots/ (retains the 5 most recent rolling snapshots). Success returns } . Message Meaning --- --- "No last-known-good state exists at ." No .bak exists; there is nothing to recover from. "The last-known-good state is also unusable: " Both primary and backup are bad; recovery fails clearly rather than guessing. "Unknown snapshot: " Specified snapshot filename does not exist in library.json.snapshots/ . Upgrading to 3.0 3.0 does not migrate a library on open. Schema 7 opens directly. A schema 6 library raises STATE_SCHEMA_TOO_OLD and is left unchanged until you run openbox --migrate-library ; the command writes library.v6.backup.json , migration-in-progress.json , and migration-report.json . A schema 1-5 library must be opened once on OpenBox 2.1 first. OpenBox 2.1.0 is the last build that restores library.v6.backup.json . 3.0 does not delete an existing v6 backup. title: Wine and Proton discovery
description: Discovers Wine prefixes and Proton runtimes on Linux and resolves the prefix recorded for a game.
body: OpenBox ships a local-first Wine and Proton discovery layer. It automatically finds existing prefixes in ~/.wine , ~/.local/share/wineprefixes , the Lutris Wine runners tree, the Faugus prefix directories, the Bottles store, and ~/Games , so you can point a title at a prefix without hand-writing a path. Heroic is not one of these sources: it appears only as a storefront importer, which is a different subsystem. Since 1.13.0 OpenBox also runs natively on Windows, where Windows titles launch directly: the Windows build does not use Wine, Proton, or UMU, and none of the discovery or launch behavior below applies there. See [Windows](/windows/) for the native Windows host, install layout, and launchers. How it works OpenBox's Wine subsystem inspects standard local directories and lists what it finds. It is a discovery and suggestion layer, not a runtime wrapper: it reads directories and reads the wine_prefix field on a game record, but it does not construct the launch command for you. 1. Prefix Discovery ( DEFAULT_PREFIX_ROOTS in crates/openbox-emulators/src/wine.rs ): - ~/.wine , ~/.local/share/wineprefixes/ - Faugus Launcher prefixes: ~/.config/faugus-launcher/prefixes , ~/Faugus - Bottles: ~/.local/share/bottles/bottles - Lutris: ~/.local/share/lutris/runners/wine - Custom folder: ~/Games - Note: ~/.local/share/lutris/runners/wine holds Wine builds , not game prefixes. The scanner only accepts a directory that actually contains a drive_c , so a runner tree is skipped even though the root is scanned. The WINEPREFIX environment variable is not a discovery root; it is only read when resolving a game's configured prefix. 2. Proton Runtime Discovery ( DEFAULT_PROTON_ROOTS in crates/openbox-emulators/src/wine.rs ): - Steam Proton: ~/.steam/root/compatibilitytools.d , ~/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d , ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d - Faugus runners: ~/.config/faugus-launcher/runners , ~/.local/share/faugus-launcher/runners - Lutris runners: ~/.local/share/lutris/runners/wine - Executables on PATH: wine , wine64 , proton , umu-run , umu-launcher - Installed Flatpak apps whose application id contains wine , proton , or faugus , reported with a flatpak: path and source flatpak Proton roots are scanned one level deep, which is why the Steam compatibilitytools.d and Lutris runner trees resolve: each direct child of a root is checked for a proton file, a files/bin/wine or dist/bin/wine binary, or a name containing "proton" or "wine". (The two-level walk belongs to the separate prefix scanner, not to this one.) Assigning a Prefix to a Game GET /api/v2/wine/prefix-for-game?game_id= resolves a title's prefix by reading the wine_prefix , prefix , or WINEPREFIX field on the game record, including a WINEPREFIX= assignment inside the launch command. There is no control for setting this, and the library API cannot set it either: the game field cleaner copies only the fields in its accepted set, and wine_prefix is not one of them, so a wine_prefix key se

title: OpenBoxGL
description: A local-first game library and launcher for Linux, Windows, and macOS.
body: OpenBox Game Launcher for Linux, Windows, and macOS One library for Steam, ROMs, and emulators. OpenBoxGL brings mixed game collections into one searchable catalog. Keep library data on your machine, enrich it with artwork and metadata, then launch and track play from the same interface. No account, no vendor cloud lock-in, no telemetry. [ Install OpenBoxGL 3.0.0 ](/install/) [ Read the quick start ](/getting-started/) [ Read the release notes ](/changelog/) What OpenBoxGL is OpenBoxGL is an open-source game library manager and launcher for Linux, Windows, and macOS. title: Installation
description: Install OpenBoxGL 3.0 on Linux with AppImage, Flatpak, or source, on Windows with the signed portable installer, or on macOS with the signed universal app bundle.
body: OpenBoxGL 3.0 runs on Linux, natively on Windows since 1.13.0, and natively on macOS since 1.19.0. Every packaged build ships the native Rust server openbox-server with no bundled Python runtime . On Linux the AppImage is the recommended path. On Windows the signed portable installer is the supported path; it is covered in full on the [Windows](/windows/) page. On macOS the signed universal app bundle installs with install-macos.sh , and the [macOS](/macos/) page covers it in full. There is no OpenBox account, installer wizard, or license key. Downloading a release or cloning the repository is the entire installation. Decide which package to use Package Best for Updates --- --- --- [AppImage]( appimage) Desktop, Steam Deck, handhelds, immutable systems Built-in verified updater [Flatpak]( flatpak) Sandboxed installs from a bundle or manifest Your normal Flatpak workflow [Source]( source--system) Development, testing, or patching git pull and rebuild [System install]( source--system) Installing to /usr/local from source sudo make install again [Windows portable]( windows) Windows 10 and 11, x86_64 or ARM64 Re-run install.ps1 from the new release [macOS]( macos) macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel Re-run install-macos.sh --replace from the new release The fastest path on Linux is the [versioned release installer]( versioned-release-installer): download the tag-pinned script, inspect it, then run it. It selects the matching AppImage, pins the release public key, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and Ed25519 signature, and installs it to ~/.local/bin . The built-in updater checks for updates on every platform, but the verified install step in the 3.0 Rust server is implemented for the AppImage only. title: Webhooks
description: Deliver signed best-effort event notifications to trusted destinations.
body: OpenBoxGL delivers signed JSON events to your own webhook endpoints when library or session events happen. Delivery is asynchronous and best-effort: it never blocks the originating operation, and a failing endpoint only records a failure. Configuration limits Limit Value --- --- Max webhook configs 32 ( MAX_WEBHOOKS ) Max URL length 2048 characters Delivery attempts 1..5 per config (default 3) Timeout per attempt 1..15 seconds (default 5) Queue 128 pending items per pool (cap 1024), 4 delivery workers Envelope size 64 KiB ( MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES ) Secret optional; when set, deliveries carry X-OpenBox-Signature Attempts and timeout are configurable per webhook and globally ( webhook_attempts , webhook_timeout in settings). Event types Event Data allowlist --- --- session.started launch_id , game_id , name , platform , started_at session.stopped launch_id , game_id , name , seconds , exit_code , timed_out , started_at , stopped_at queue.advanced from_game_id , from_entry_id , to_game_id , to_entry_id library.imported source , found , added library.changed action , game_ids , count metadata.synced status backup.created archive_name , items update.installed version plugin.changed action , plugin Data payloads are allowlisted per event: any other key in the caller-provided data is dropped before the envelope is built. You cannot smuggle extra fields through. Envelope and signature Every delivery is a compact JSON POST: Headers: Content-Type: application/json , User-Agent: OpenBox/1 , X-OpenBox-Event-Id , X-OpenBox-Event , X-OpenBox-Timestamp , and X-OpenBox-Signature: sha256= when the config has a secret. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + "." + body where body is the exact transmitted JSON bytes. Verify it as: URL validation POST /api/v2/webhooks and POST /api/v2/webhooks/test reject unsafe targets before saving: - Scheme must be https by default. Plain http is refused unless OPENBOX_ALLOW_HTTP_WEBHOOKS=1 is set for trusted local testing. - No embedded credentials, no fragments, port within 1..65535. - The host must resolve; unspecified, multicast, link-local, and reserved addresses are rejected. - Loopback destinations must not be the running OpenBoxGL server (matched by port and by a live TCP probe), so the app cannot webhook itself into a loop. Delivery behavior - A matching enabled config receives the envelope for every subscribed event. - Retryable statuses: 408, 425, 429, and any 5xx. Backoff is exponential (1, 2, 4, 8 seconds); a Retry-After header raises the wait as a floor, capped at 30 seconds. - Redirects (3xx) are a terminal failure: a redirected request is never followed, because following would send the signed payload to an unvalidated destination. - Response bodies are drained with a bounded read (4 KiB) and discarded; the response body, resolved addresses, and credentials are never surfaced. - A full delivery queue drops the event with a failure notification ( "Webhook delivery queue is full; the event was dropped." ). - Deliv

title: Interfaces and data
description: Understand OpenBoxGL interfaces, local state, and environment selection.
body: OpenBoxGL ships one UI over two hosts that share one local library. This page explains what you see, how the pieces fit together, and exactly where your data lives so you can back it up, move it, or diagnose problems. One UI, two hosts Host Entry point What you see Best for --- --- --- --- Native window openbox or openbox-native A native WebKitGTK window rendering the same three-column workspace: filter sidebar, cover grid or list, detail pane Default desktop use Web UI openbox --web (Rust server) The same UI in a browser tab Development, debugging, REST API, Big Box mode Both hosts render the identical index.html , app.js , and app.css served by the loopback server, so there is no second presentation stack to drift. The native host is a small C/Objective-C shim that owns the window chrome and spawns openbox-server as a child; it never contains application logic. The Python web_app.py path is the OPENBOX_BACKEND=python fallback. Native host Starting openbox (or openbox-native ) does three things in order: 1. Acquires a single-instance lock; a second launch focuses the existing window and exits. 2. Spawns openbox-server --no-browser (or python3 web_app.py --no-browser when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python ) as a child and waits for it to write server.port and server.token . 3. Opens a WebKitGTK window at http://127.0.0.1:PORT/?token=... , restores the last window geometry, and registers a window.openboxNative bridge for native dialogs, external opens, reveal, and window chrome. On window close the host shuts the server down cleanly. When WebKitGTK is missing, the launcher prints an install hint and falls back to the system-browser app window, so no install bricks. The bridge surface is window.openboxNative , injected by native_host.c on Linux, native_host_win.c on Windows, and native_host_mac.m on macOS: Member Purpose --- --- dialog(kind, opts) Native file open/save dialogs (C handle_dialog ) reveal(path) Reveal a data/home-contained path in the file manager (containing folder only; never launches it) openExternal(target) Open an approved external URL in the system handler windowAction(action) Native window chrome actions (minimize, focus, geometry) onGamepad(callback) Gamepad-input hook (no-op stub in the current host) Web UI Running openbox --web starts the Rust loopback server and prints a tokenless URL; open it with ?token= or drive the API with X-OpenBox-Token . python3 web_app.py is the Python fallback and requires OPENBOX_BACKEND=python (or no Rust binary). The server is loopback-only, so nothing is reachable from the network. The URL carries the per-launch token in the query string; the API also accepts the same value as an X-OpenBox-Token header. When the server stops, both files are deleted. The keyboard launcher ( scripts/openbox-launcher.sh ) and openbox:// deep links read these two files to find and authenticate against the running server. See [Command line and deep links](/reference/cli/) for the full flag and URI reference. Where data lives

title: Localization
description: OpenBox ships in 5 languages. How the i18n system works, and how to add more.
body: Localization OpenBox ships locale catalogs for English, Spanish, German, French, and Portuguese . The locale selector is in Settings Interface language ; switching re-translates the keyed UI surfaces without a page reload. Some operational and browser fallback labels remain English. How it works The i18n system uses three layers: 1. Locale files : JSON files in locales/ .json with a nested key structure (e.g. nav.library , sidebar.search , settings.title ). 2. HTML translation : data-i18n="key" attributes on translatable elements; data-i18n-placeholder , data-i18n-title , and data-i18n-aria-label for attribute translation. 3. JS translation : t(key, params) from static/i18n.js with interpolation and automatic English fallback for missing keys. The locale is loaded via fetch('/locales/ .json') on page load, with en.json as the canonical fallback. The available locales are exposed in public_settings as available_locales . Gate enforcement scripts/check_i18n.py runs on every make check and verifies: - All 5 locale files have 100% key coverage (no missing keys in any locale). - All data-i18n and t() references in the codebase have corresponding keys in en.json . - No locale file carries extra keys outside en.json : an extra key fails the gate the same way a missing key does. A locale file with missing keys will fail CI. This prevents shipping partial translations. The gate verifies key and placeholder parity, not translation quality. 1.18.0 copy still in English In es , de , fr , and pt , the 1.18.0 additions are present with the same keys and placeholders but are still English strings in this release: the renamed and newly added Tools entries (including the four group headings and their 17 hints), the Add games menu, the new top-bar labels, and the new setup, help, onboarding, and Jump back in copy. That is 52 of the 55 renamed or new tools. and nav. keys per locale, plus the new setup, help, onboarding, and Add games copy. Untouched entries keep their existing translations, and a native-copy translation pass follows. Adding a new language 1. Create locales/ .json with the same key structure as locales/en.json . 2. Add the locale code to SUPPORTED_LOCALES in static/i18n.js . 3. Add the locale to the public GET list in crates/openbox-http/src/middleware.rs and SUPPORTED_LOCALES in static/i18n.js . 4. Add the locale to PUBLIC_GET_PATHS in routes.py . 5. Add the locale to available_locales in crates/openbox-http/src/handlers/projection.rs . 6. Run python3 scripts/check_i18n.py to verify 100% key coverage. 7. Run make check to verify the full gate passes. Each entry in available_locales carries both a plain name and a native name, but the picker renders only the native one — the option label is the native name, falling back to the plain name and then the code. So the shipped list shows English , Español , Deutsch , Français , and Português ; the plain names ( English , Spanish , German , French , Portuguese ) exist in the payload but are never displayed

title: macOS
description: Install and run OpenBoxGL on macOS 11 or newer with the signed universal app bundle, the install script, and the WKWebView window.
body: OpenBoxGL runs natively on macOS 11 or newer, on Apple Silicon and Intel, since 1.19.0. The release is one signed universal app bundle, OpenBox-macos.zip (17.4 MiB), which ships the Rust openbox-server and renders the UI in a WKWebView window with no bundled Python. The library format, the web UI, the HTTP API, the plugins, and the emulator definitions are the same as on Linux and Windows, so a library directory moves between platforms unchanged. The macOS build hides Linux-only controls instead of failing when you click them. The list is in [What is not on macOS]( what-is-not-on-macos). Requirements Requirement Needed for Notes --- --- --- macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel Everything One universal bundle serves both. The bundle declares a minimum system version of 11.0. python3 on PATH , version 3.11 or newer install-macos.sh only The installer runs the release verifier with python3 . The Command Line Tools python3 can be older than 3.11; brew install python@3.12 is the usual fix. The installed app does not use this interpreter. curl , shasum , ditto install-macos.sh only Ship with macOS. WKWebView The native window Ships with macOS. Rust 1.92 or newer Source builds The app bundle ships the Rust server, so the installed app needs nothing. Python 3.11+ is only for the OPENBOX_BACKEND=python fallback and .py plugins. Install the app bundle Download install-macos.sh from the release, read it, and run it with the tag pinned. The script checks the release public key against the trust anchor pinned inside the script, verifies the bundle's SHA-256 checksum and Ed25519 signature, then installs OpenBox.app : What the installer does: - Installs OpenBox.app into ~/Applications . Set OPENBOX_INSTALL_DIR to install somewhere else. - Links the openbox launcher into ~/.local/bin . If that folder is not on your PATH , the installer says so. - Refuses to replace an existing OpenBox.app unless you pass --replace , for example bash install-macos.sh --replace . - Resolves the latest release only when you omit OPENBOX_RELEASE_TAG . Omit it only when you intend to track the latest release. First launch: allow the app The bundle is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. The first time you open it, macOS asks you to allow it. Open System Settings Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway . Every new build asks again, because each build has a new ad-hoc signature. The release signature is what the installer and the in-app updater verify; the ad-hoc signature only shows that the bundle was not changed after it was built. Launching OpenBox Command What it does --- --- openbox Opens the native WKWebView window. openbox --web Starts the same local server and opens the UI in your browser. title: Privacy
description: What OpenBox does and does not collect, and how its data stays on your machine.
body: Privacy OpenBox is designed so your library, saves, and metadata never leave your machine unless you explicitly trigger something. This page says exactly what that means and where the boundaries are. What OpenBox does not do - No telemetry. No analytics beacons, no crash reports, no usage statistics are sent anywhere. There is nothing to opt out of. - No account. There is no OpenBox account, no login, no license key. Downloading the AppImage or cloning the repository is the entire installation. - No cloud library. Library data lives in library.json on your machine. The local server binds to 127.0.0.1 only and every API request must carry a per-launch token, so the window (or tab) you open is the only client. - No hidden network calls. The app does not phone home at startup. The only scheduled outbound feature is opt-in Deal Radar, which polls https://store.steampowered.com at the interval you set. What leaves your machine, and when Most outbound actions are user-initiated and visible in the UI. Deal Radar is the one opt-in scheduled exception: - LaunchBox metadata database. Downloading or updating the LaunchBox metadata database fetches the archive from gamesdb.launchbox-app.com and builds a local SQLite copy. OpenBox then matches titles locally against that database, so no game title or library entry is sent for an individual lookup. The download happens when you trigger it — for example after an import, or from the metadata screen. - IGDB search. A search you type is sent to IGDB. IGDB API failures surface readable errors. - ScreenScraper and SteamGridDB. Metadata and artwork lookups you trigger send the game title, platform, and identifiers to those services under your own account or API key. - Gameyfin. Connecting a Gameyfin server sends the configured URL and library requests to that server. - RetroAchievements. Your username and API key, plus ROM hashes for matching, go to RetroAchievements when you use that integration. The key is stored locally in a 0o600 file. - Steam achievements and playtime. If you configure a Steam Web API key and Steam ID, OpenBox reads achievement and playtime totals from api.steampowered.com . The request carries those identifiers, not your library files. - EmuMovies. Media downloads authenticate with your EmuMovies credentials. - Netplay lobby. Opening Online play fetches RetroArch's public HTTPS lobby listing. No credentials are sent, and RetroArch itself makes the room connection. - Webhooks. If you configure webhooks, event deliveries go to the URLs you specify, signed with your HMAC secret. Destinations are validated against loopback and local address rules before anything is sent. - Statistics sync. If you enable it, play statistics sync to a local folder you choose (for example a Syncthing folder). You control the destination. - Deal Radar. If you enable it ( deals_enabled ), OpenBox queries https://store.steampowered.com for the app ids on your watchlist at deals_poll_hours (default 168). Requests and redi

title: Security
description: Report vulnerabilities and protect local OpenBoxGL data.
body: Reporting a vulnerability Do not report security vulnerabilities in public issues. Use the [private GitHub security advisory form](https://github.com/vindeckyy/OpenBoxGL/security/advisories/new). If advisories are unavailable, open a minimal public issue asking for a private contact channel without disclosing exploit details. Include the issue description and impact, reproduction steps, affected version(s), a proof of concept if available, and a suggested remediation. Maintainers aim to acknowledge valid reports within 5 business days and provide a remediation plan or status update within 14 business days. Fixed in 1.16.0: what 1.15.x and earlier are exposed to If you run 1.15.x or older, these are the security defects 1.16.0 closes. None of them is backported, so upgrading is the fix. - Arbitrary .json read through a crafted preview_id . The import setup preview and the Launch Doctor joined the request's preview_id into a file path without checking it, so a ../ -laden id returned any JSON file on disk, settings.json with your provider credentials included. Every preview_id now goes through one identifier validator and a containment check. - Arbitrary file write through a game's rom_name . Restoring a high-score bundle built the destination filename from rom_name , so a traversal string wrote outside the high-score folder. The name is reduced to a safe component and the destination is checked to stay inside that folder. - Plugins reading your library. The plugin sandbox masked a fixed list of paths, so if you had moved your OpenBox data folder with OPENBOX_DATA_DIR , a sandboxed plugin could read library.json and settings.json . The resolved data directory is now hidden from plugins wherever it lives. - Unescaped text in the Wrapped report. Game names reached the page without escaping. Your CSP blocked script execution, so this was one policy change away from being exploitable rather than exploitable directly; names are escaped now, and an automated check fails if the pattern returns. - An outside package changing how your library is saved. The shipped runtime is the Rust openbox-server with a pinned dependency lockfile and cargo deny in CI. The Python fallback is standard-library only, and an automated check enforces it. Testing Run the full suite before submitting a pull request: Each test_ .py is a standalone contract test (plain asserts or unittest) run directly with python3 -B .
