title: Releasing
description: Cut and publish an OpenBox release and its verified artifacts.
body: This page is for maintainers publishing a release from master . The AppImage, Windows portable, macOS app bundle, and Flatpak artifacts are built in CI when a v tag is pushed; the steps below prepare the version, changelog, and metadata before that tag. Before you tag 1. Work from a clean master that tracks origin/master ; confirm the target tag does not already exist. 2. Bump updates.py VERSION to the new semver. 3. Add a dated section to docs/CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog format) and the comparison links, and update docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md (CI publishes it as the release body). 4. Prepend release metadata to openbox.metainfo.xml . 5. Update the README release badge, PARITY.md latest-release text, the bug-report template's version field, and any branch/version references that should track the current release. Review SUPPORT.md , the Flathub checklist, installer architecture examples, and this page. Leave historical version references in old changelog/metainfo entries and completed specs unchanged. 6. Run the local gates: Build and verify the artifact locally Prerequisites: Rust 1.92+ (the pinned toolchain is 1.99.1), gcc , pkg-config , and the WebKitGTK dev package ( libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev on Debian/Ubuntu, webkit2gtk-4.1 on Fedora). The build compiles openbox-server with Cargo and native_host.c against webkit2gtk-4.1 , and bundles no Python interpreter. OPENBOX_ARCH overrides architecture detection ( x86_64 or aarch64 ); the output is OpenBox-$arch.AppImage (default OpenBox-x86_64.AppImage ). Build each architecture separately when testing locally: The build produces the architecture-specific AppImage and .zsync pair, but does not regenerate the .sha256 sidecar. Regenerate it explicitly: Confirm the embedded version matches the release with openbox-server --dump-contracts (or GET /api/v2/version from the running build). updates.py is a build-time/installer file and is not installed into the AppDir. Push and tag 1. Commit the version/changelog/metadata changes, push directly to master , and wait for the Rust workspace checks and the Python 3.11/3.12 CI jobs to pass for that exact commit. 2. Create and push an annotated tag: What CI does Pushing a v tag triggers the AppImage/Windows release workflow and the Flatpak release workflow. The two publish jobs share a per-tag concurrency group because both update the same GitHub Release. release.yml defines ten jobs: test , build , attest , build-windows , attest-windows , build-windows-arm64 , attest-windows-arm64 , build-macos , attest-macos , and one shared publish . body: OpenBox 1.18.0 adds 49 method and path pairs across 43 routes , all additive. No v1 route was removed, renamed, or re-mapped: the frozen contract still pins the same 61 /api/v1/ routes, and the route baseline's retired list is empty. The new routes either extend an existing base path ( /api/v2/media/queue now reports the durable queue in full) or add a local-workflow path under /api and /api/v2 . None of them gained a /api/v1/ alias. The additions cluster around seven jobs: administering platforms in one place, keeping media downloads and cache under control, making saves inspectable before a restore, giving achievements and plugins durable state, scanning storefronts and importing the long tail of formats, storing optional service credentials privately, and driving the emulator and native-host surfaces. Use X-OpenBox-Token: TOKEN in scripts. POST bodies are JSON objects and are subject to the shared 65,536-byte body limit. Routes that resolve a game accept a stable game_id first and fall back to a numeric id index when no stable id is present; a payload that cannot be resolved returns 400 with "Game not found" . title: REST API overview
description: Loopback boundary, authentication, body limits, and the request lifecycle.
body: The Rust server ( openbox-server ) binds to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, or the port in OPENBOX_PORT . This page documents the shared contract every route follows and the lifecycle a request goes through. Route lists live on the group pages. The public surface is /api/v2/ ; the native windows use /api/host/ . Loopback boundary - The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, so nothing is reachable from the network. OPENBOX_PORT can pin the port; the default is 0 . - OpenBoxGL does not terminate HTTPS. Use a trusted network and an external reverse proxy if you must expose it beyond the host. - Requests carry a 30-second timeout. - The public GET surface is / , /index.html , /static/ .js .svg , /static/app.css , /static/logo.png , /assets/placeholder-cover.svg , /locales/ .json , /favicon.ico , and /favicon.svg . Every other route requires authentication. Authentication All API routes require the session token. The server writes it to server.token in the data directory at startup and deletes the file on exit. Two transports are accepted: - Header: X-OpenBox-Token: TOKEN (preferred) - Query parameter: ?token=TOKEN (can leak through history and logs) The token is compared in constant time. Authentication runs before the host-version guard, the retired-route guard, and route resolution, so an unknown route without a token returns 403 , not 404 . A missing or wrong token returns 403 . Ten failures in 60 seconds per IP return 429 with code: "RATE_LIMITED" , retry_after , and a Retry-After header; a correct token clears the bucket. Request lifecycle A request flows through a fixed set of stages. Knowing the order tells you which status code you will get and why: Most structured error responses carry a stable code and a request_id . The request id is a short per-request token that also appears in the diagnostic log, so a screenshot of an error banner can be correlated with the log line. Since 2.0, every error response is an application/problem+json (RFC 9457) document carrying type , title , status , detail , code , retryable , request_id , and instance ; the error field is kept as a duplicate of detail for one compatibility cycle. The payload examples in the table below show the fields older integrations read; the full document adds the problem-details members on top. Handlers return a typed ApiError ; validation failures are 400 with a readable detail , and state errors are mapped before the handler runs ( 409 for schema-too-old, future, or frozen; 503 for corrupt state). An unhandled failure is logged and returned as 500 with a request_id . This is why almost every operation failure you hit through the API is a 400 with a readable, specific message, and why a 500 is genuinely "something the developers need to see," not a normal error path. Bodies - POST bodies must be JSON. Bodies over 65,536 bytes are rejected with "Request is too large." ; truncated bodies with "Request body was truncated." . - The body must decode to a JSON object; [] , null , "text" , and

title: API 2.1 changes
description: The 2.1 contract — /api/v2-only dispatch, retired-surface 410 documents, the cursor jobs panel, and backup format 1 write retirement.
body: 2.1 made the 2.0 contracts permanent. The public API is /api/v2 only; unversioned /api/ paths are no longer dispatched, /api/v1 is removed, and the legacy native-host names are gone. Backups write format 2 only, and the jobs panel reads the cursor-based v2 list. v2-only dispatch Request Result in 2.1 and later --- --- /api/v2/ Dispatched. /api/host/ Dispatched to the native-window channel after the API-version guard. /api/v1/ 410 V1_API_REMOVED with detail.use pointing at /api/v2 . /api/launch , /api/shutdown , /api/native/capabilities 410 HOST_CHANNEL_RETIRED with the replacement host path. Any other /api/ path with a /api/v2 twin 410 API_VERSION_REQUIRED with detail.use pointing at the v2 path. Any other /api/ path with no v2 twin 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND . OPENBOX_ENABLE_V1_API is ignored with a startup warning. Retired paths authenticate before they return their 410 , so an unauthenticated caller still receives 403 . Jobs panel GET /api/v2/jobs returns a cursor list, not the old job-name map: Query parameters: limit (default 50, max 100), cursor , type or type_filter , state or state_filter , root_job_id , and group_by=root_job_id . Per-operation rows are at GET /api/v2/jobs/items?job_id=… . POST /api/v2/jobs/cancel , /retry , and /resume return 202 with the updated job row. The legacy job-name map and GET /api/jobs are gone. Backups Format 2 is the only writable format. Format 1 archives still restore. A new format 1 write returns 410 BACKUP_FORMAT_RETIRED with the message "Backup format 1 is no longer written by OpenBox 2.1. Use a 2.0.x build to create a 1.19-compatible export." Turning it off skips manifest writes and media hashing; the integrity report says the manifest is disabled instead of reporting every file as untracked. See [Configuration](/reference/configuration/). The unversioned request path is no longer a second way in. Related pages - [API 2.0 changes](/reference/api/two-zero/) - [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/) - [Updating](/updating/)

title: API 2.0 changes
description: The 2.0 contract surface — /api/v2 becomes the public API, /api/v1 retires behind an opt-in bridge, the /api/host channel, problem+json errors, and the migration, portable-library, and version routes.
body: This page records the 2.0 contract. The current release is 3.0.0. The /api/v1 bridge described here was removed in 2.1, and 3.0 moved the server to Rust. See [API 2.1 changes](/reference/api/two-one/) and [API 3.0 changes](/reference/api/three-zero/). OpenBox 2.0 promoted /api/v2 from an additive surface to the public API, retired /api/v1 behind an opt-in bridge, gave the native windows their own /api/host channel, and answered every error as an RFC 9457 problem document. It added 10 routes and 3 settings ( library_root , path_mode , media_manifest_enabled ). Every route still requires the per-launch token described in the [API overview](/reference/api/overview/). The public API is /api/v2 /api/v2 and /api/host are the supported surfaces. In 2.0 /api/v1 was off by default ; it was removed entirely in 2.1. Surface State in 2.0 State in 3.0 --- --- --- /api/v2/ The public API. Everything new lands here. The public API. /api/host/ The native-window channel. Guarded by X-OpenBox-API-Version (below). The native-window channel. /api/v1/ Off by default. OPENBOX_ENABLE_V1_API=1 restored it through 2.0.x. Removed: 410 V1_API_REMOVED ; the environment variable is ignored. The frozen 61-route v1 list is archived at docs/archive/v1_contracts.json in the app repo; the live route contract is api_contracts.json , enforced by scripts/check_api_contract.py . The host channel The native windows (WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS) talk to /api/host/ and send X-OpenBox-API-Version: 2 . A window that sends a different major version is refused before the route runs with 409 HOST_API_UNSUPPORTED and the message "This OpenBox window is from a different version. Restart OpenBox and the window together." A request with no version header is not refused. Problem-details errors Every error response (status 400 and up) is now an RFC 9457 problem document served as application/problem+json : - type is derived from code ( https://openbox.local/problems/ + the lowercased code with dashes). - code is the stable machine-readable key; it survives rewording of detail / title . - error duplicates detail for one major cycle, so existing clients keep working. - retryable is true for 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, and for any payload that carries retry_after . Version and contract report GET /api/v2/version reports every contract version so a client can refuse a shape it cannot read: GET /api/v2/compat/report serves the same deterministic compatibility report as Settings → About → Show compatibility report : the library format, each theme's token fallbacks, which backup formats restore on which version, unknown settings keys, the public API and host channel, and the sync folder. Migration gate In 2.0 a format 6 library was upgraded on first start. In 3.0 opening does not migrate: run openbox --migrate-library first. A readiness gate then lists what needs a look before the migrated library is used. The four routes back it: Route Behavior --- --- GET /api/v2/

title: REST API
description: Use the local authenticated HTTP API for automation.
body: The app exposes a local REST API for automation and third-party tooling. The Rust server ( openbox-server ) binds to loopback only and requires a per-launch token on every request. The public surface is /api/v2/ ; the native windows use /api/host/ . Unversioned /api/ paths were retired in 2.1 and /api/v1 was removed in 2.1. This page is the index; each operation group has its own reference page, and [How OpenBoxGL works](/reference/how-it-works/) explains the server, the error contract, and the lifecycle. Quickstart Find your token and port, then call any route with the X-OpenBox-Token header: Replace GAME_ID with a real game- id from /api/v2/library . The token and port live only while the app is running; both files are deleted when the server stops. ?token=TOKEN works but leaks into browser history, referrer logs, and proxy logs. Use X-OpenBox-Token in anything you write. Server and transport - The API listens at http://127.0.0.1:SERVER_PORT on a random port chosen at startup. The port and token are written to server.port and server.token inside the data directory and deleted when the server stops. - OpenBoxGL does not terminate HTTPS. The API is designed for the local host. If you expose it beyond the machine, put a trusted reverse proxy in front and understand the trust boundary first. - Requests time out after 30 seconds at the socket level. - JSON request bodies are limited to 65,536 bytes. A larger body returns HTTP 400 with a problem document whose detail is "Request is too large.". Authentication Every route except the static UI, locale JSON, and other explicitly public assets requires a token. Send it as a header: The query parameter token=TOKEN is also accepted but can leak through browser history, referrer logs, and proxy logs. Prefer the header in anything you write. The app scrubs ?token= from history immediately ( history.replaceState ) and never logs the token-bearing URL; logs use the token-free http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ . The token is compared in constant time. Authentication runs before host-version checks, retired-route guards, and route resolution, so an unknown route without a token returns 403 , not 404 . A missing or wrong token returns 403 with . Ten failures in 60 seconds per IP return 429 with code: "RATE_LIMITED" and a Retry-After header; a correct token clears the bucket. Response envelope Most API handlers return JSON objects. Since 2.0 every error is served as application/problem+json (RFC 9457) carrying type , title , status , detail , a stable code , retryable , request_id , and instance ; error is kept as a duplicate of detail for one compatibility cycle. The payloads below name the fields integrations read today. Public assets, media/download endpoints, and Server-Sent Events can return bytes or streams instead of JSON. The versioned route pages document the response shape for each operation. Status Meaning --- --- 200 Success 202 Accepted; a background job was started (metadata sync, media bulk, emulator install/u

title: System Architecture & Reliability
description: The Rust openbox-server, native window hosts, the JSON state store, background operations, and the Python fallback boundary.
body: OpenBox is engineered as a local-first, single-binary application. The shipped backend is the native Rust server openbox-server ; the native window hosts are thin platform shells that render the same HTML/CSS/JS UI over loopback. There is no OpenBox account, vendor cloud dependency, or background telemetry service. Core architectural layers 1. Rust server, zero bundled CPython openbox-server is built from the Cargo workspace in crates/ (15 crates, 170 migrated backend modules, 417 HTTP endpoints: 413 public /api/v2/ plus 4 /api/host/ ). It uses Tokio, Axum/Hyper, rusqlite for the derived read model, and ed25519-dalek for release verification. The AppImage, Flatpak, Windows zips, and the macOS .app ship this binary directly; no Python interpreter is bundled. - Binds to 127.0.0.1 only, on an ephemeral port or OPENBOX_PORT . - Publishes server.port , server.token , and native-host-flags in the data directory with owner-only permissions. - Every non-public request requires X-OpenBox-Token ; the token is compared in constant time and auth failures are rate-limited. - The AppImage keeps a GLIBC_2.35 floor (Ubuntu 22.04). The Python tree ( web_app.py , handlers/ , pkg/ ) still exists for source checkouts. It runs only when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python is set or no Rust binary is found, and it requires Python 3.11 or newer. 2. Native host and IPC bridge The native hosts are deliberately thin: Platform Host Webview Server supervision --- --- --- --- Linux native_host.c WebKitGTK 4.1 / GTK 3 fork + setpgid , execl(openbox-server --no-browser) , inotify boot watch, process-group shutdown Windows native_host_win.c WebView2 / Win32 CreateProcessW in a job object, graceful /api/host/shutdown , TerminateJobObject backstop macOS native_host_mac.m WKWebView / AppKit posix_spawn with process group, DISPATCH_PROC_EXIT monitor, 0600 AF_UNIX socket All three hosts resolve openbox-server in the order OPENBOX_SERVER_BIN → bundle/share → target/release → PATH , and fall back to python3 web_app.py only when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python is set. They inject window.openboxNative for native dialogs, reveal/open-external actions, and window controls, and they use /api/host/ for launch, resume, shutdown, and capabilities. 3. Atomic state store and recovery library.json is the canonical schema 7 state. The store in crates/openbox-store/src/json_store.rs provides: - Atomic writes: a temporary file is flushed, fsynced, and atomically renamed; the previous primary is kept as library.json.bak . - Snapshots: rotating library.json.snapshots/ - - .json files, newest-first, capped at 5. Snapshotting uses hardlinks where possible. - Locking: an in-process ordered mutex plus a cross-process sidecar lock. Windows uses a byte-range lock; POSIX uses flock . - Crash recovery: a corrupt primary falls back to .bak ; POST /api/v2/state/recover reports what would be recovered and can snapshot first. - Schema policy: schema 7 opens directly. Schema 6 raises STATE_SCHEMA_TOO_OLD and is not rewritten on open;

title: Background jobs
description: Observable states, retry limits, replacement, cancellation, and volatility.
body: Background work in OpenBoxGL runs through the durable Operation Service in crates/openbox-store/src/operations.rs . Operations are persisted to operations.json plus one operations_items/ .json per job, surviving application restarts and supporting progress streaming, cancellation, retries, and resume flows. The Python crates/openbox-store/src/operations.rs path remains only for OPENBOX_BACKEND=python . The operation object Every submitted operation is recorded with these fields: Key Meaning --- --- job_id Unique hex identifier root_job_id Identifier of the root job a retry or resume descends from retry_of job_id of the job this one retries resume_of job_id of the job this one resumes type Dotted operation type (see supported types below) title Human-readable job title state queued , running , cancelling , done , partial , error , cancelled , or interrupted phase Current phase label current Progress counter total Progress total message Progress or status message created_at UTC ISO timestamp updated_at Last change timestamp started_at Start timestamp finished_at Terminal timestamp can_cancel Whether the job can be cancelled right now can_retry Whether the job can be retried right now can_resume Whether the job can be resumed right now input Context-specific parameters, with secrets redacted checkpoint Resume checkpoint data result Result counters, normalised to added , merged , skipped , excluded , failed , completed , downloaded error Error object on failure ( code , message , request_id ) Progress is flat: phase , current , total , and message are top-level keys, and there is no unit field. Supported operation types Jobs carry a dotted type : setup.scan , setup.revalidate , setup.commit , metadata.db_sync , metadata.match_preview , metadata.match_auto , metadata.apply , metadata.media_auto , media.bulk_download , media.cleanup , media.memories_import , emulator.install , emulator.update , gameyfin.install , saves.scan , saves.backup , saves.restore , library.backup , library.restore , library.export , screenscraper.match , screenscraper.apply , steamgrid.match , steamgrid.apply , storefront.auto_import , storefront.scan , clips.reel , cloud.sync , updater.install , trail.refresh , and itinerary.igdb . The legacy job-name map was removed in 2.1; the v2 list returns typed rows. At most MAX_OPERATIONS=100 operations are retained. Workers run as Tokio blocking tasks behind a semaphore with 4 concurrent slots ( DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS=4 ). Live status and incremental events stream to the frontend over Server-Sent Events (SSE) via /api/v2/events . States and lifecycle transitions - queued : Submitted and awaiting execution slot. - running : Actively executing in a worker thread. - cancelling : User requested cancellation; worker is safely terminating. - cancelled : Worker terminated early without side-effect leaks. - done : Operation completed successfully. - partial : Operation completed with some skipped or non-fatal item errors. - error : Unrecoverable

title: Command line and deep links
description: Launch OpenBox from a terminal, script backups, and drive the app with openbox:// deep links.
body: Command line and deep links OpenBox is a local app, so the command line is a first-class surface. The shipped launchers ( openbox , openbox-native , openbox.cmd , openbox.ps1 ) start the Rust openbox-server and the native window. This page covers the flags the current release accepts, the Python-fallback-only flags, and the openbox:// URI scheme. Entry points Command What it starts --- --- openbox The native window (default) openbox-native The native window (the same host) openbox --web The Rust server without a native window; prints a tokenless loopback URL openbox-server The Rust server directly (headless) The native window renders the same UI as the web fallback; both serve index.html over the loopback server. The launchers resolve openbox-server first ( OPENBOX_SERVER_BIN , bundle/share, target/release , then PATH ) and fall back to python3 web_app.py only when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python is set or no Rust binary exists. On macOS, openbox is the launcher inside OpenBox.app , which install-macos.sh links into ~/.local/bin . The native window is WKWebView, and openbox --web serves the same UI without a window. Flags Flags marked server are implemented by openbox-server ; pass them through openbox --web or invoke openbox-server directly. Flags marked launcher are handled by openbox.sh / the native host. Flags marked Python fallback work only when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python runs web_app.py . Flag Behavior --- --- -h , --help server — print usage and exit. openbox --help is forwarded to the native host and does not print OpenBox usage; use openbox --web --help or openbox-server --help . --web launcher — start the server without a native window. The server prints http://127.0.0.1: / (no token); open it with ?token= or send X-OpenBox-Token . --no-browser server — suppress browser auto-launch. The server is always headless; the native host passes this flag. The native window ignores it. --game-mode server — Steam Game Mode / gamescope guest mode. Linux only: on Windows and macOS the server exits with status 2 and prints Game Mode needs gamescope and is only available on Linux. The native window ignores the flag and detects gamescope from the environment. --play server — launch a game by stable game_id or numeric library id. Without an id, prints usage and exits with status 2. --uri server — dispatch a deep link against a running instance (or start one) and exit. A bare openbox://... positional argument is also accepted. --launcher server — run the keyboard quick launcher. The shipped scripts/openbox-launcher.sh still queries the retired unversioned paths ( /api/launcher/menu , /api/launch ); use the versioned routes directly until the helper is updated. --backup [--items a,b] server — create a backup archive and print its path. --items takes a comma-separated list of library , settings , media , plugins , themes , and extension_data ; unknown names are ignored, and the default is library,settings . The CLI does not implement --keep ; use the API keep field or

title: Command tokens
description: Use exact placeholders in emulator and launch profile commands.
body: Launch commands are tokenized strings: OpenBoxGL substitutes exact placeholders into argv, never through a shell. This page documents every token, how substitution works, and the errors you can hit. Tokens The Rust launch engine resolves the command in crates/openbox-emulators/src/defs.rs ( resolve_launch ) and applies tokens in tokens.rs ( build_launch_args ). The Python openbox.py / crates/openbox-emulators / crates/openbox-emulators/src/tokens.rs path is the OPENBOX_BACKEND=python fallback. The command is split with the platform's quoting rules first: POSIX shell quoting on Linux and macOS, and Windows command-line quoting on Windows. Markers are then replaced inside each resulting argument: Token Value Example --- --- --- (aliases , ) Absolute path to the game file, ROM, or extracted archive member /home/you/roms/zelda.nes (alias ) Parent directory containing the game file or ROM /home/you/roms (alias ) Filename with extension zelda.nes (alias ) Filename without extension zelda (alias ) Game title from the library entry The Legend of Zelda (alias ) Platform name NES ROM filename (for example, the MAME set name or archive member name) zelda Steam application ID ( steam_app_id field) 22380 Heroic application ID ( heroic_app_id field) 1091500 Lutris game identifier ( lutris_id field) 1 Parent directory of the resolved emulator executable /usr/bin Core file name the game uses (v1.16.1+), expanded from the emulator definition before anything else. Set by choosing a per-game core in Launch check, or left empty to use the definition's default. The per-platform emulator_platform_settings override is applied by the Python fallback only; the Rust launch engine does not consume it yet. snes9x_libretro.so OpenBox user data directory /home/you/.local/share/openbox-game-launcher is a plain alias of and substitutes the same value. The append heuristic is case-insensitive, so is recognised and the path is not appended a second time. Quick Resume state tokens (v1.11.0+) Emulator-def state: templates can use these additional tokens, resolved per game when a Quick Resume state is saved or restored. They are meaningless in an ordinary launch command and substitute empty there: Token Value Example consumer --- --- --- Absolute path of the emulator state file OpenBox manages for the game Dolphin --save_state= , PPSSPP --state= Per-game directory OpenBox manages for state files MAME -state_directory State name OpenBox assigns inside the state directory MAME -state Path to the generated adapter config fragment (RetroArch auto-save into state_dir , command net enabled) RetroArch --appendconfig When a game has no per-game launch command, resolution walks the precedence chain: a matching emulator adapter from emulator_defs/ first, then the platform profile from profiles , then platform detection. The definition packs and discover_profiles provide defaults such as dosbox , dolphin-emu -b -e , and pcsx2-qt . A per-game launch_profile is applied by the Python fallback onl

title: Configuration
description: Configure environment values, local state, and application settings.
body: OpenBoxGL reads configuration from three places: the process environment, discovered .env files, and persisted application settings (the Settings dialog). A .env file is a credential and HTTP-allowlist file only — it never carries general settings. This page documents each source, the exact variables, and the validation limits applied when settings are saved. Configuration sources Source When it is read Precedence --- --- --- Process environment At startup and on demand ( os.environ ) Highest for every variable it defines Discovered .env files bootstrap_env at Web UI startup, lazily before some lookups Never overrides an existing environment value Persisted settings library.json - settings Provider-specific (see below); the only store for UI settings A .env file sets an environment variable only when that variable is not already set, so the process environment always wins. Unreadable or non-UTF-8 .env files are skipped silently; an optional .env must never abort startup. A .env file is a credential and HTTP-allowlist file only. openbox-io/src/env_config.rs loads just the names in ENV_KEYS : the provider credentials, the GitHub token aliases, OPENBOX_ALLOW_HTTP_WEBHOOKS , and OPENBOX_ALLOW_HTTP_GAMEYFIN . Every other key in the file is dropped silently, so .env cannot carry general settings. Credential precedence Precedence is per provider, not one global order: Provider Order --- --- RetroAchievements retroachievements.json in the data directory, then the environment EmuMovies emumovies.json in the data directory, then the environment Steam /steam.json wins per field; STEAM_API_KEY / STEAM_ID only fill the values the file does not have IGDB, ScreenScraper, SteamGridDB Environment only Gameyfin Settings only ( library.json ); no environment variables .env discovery order openbox-io checks these roots in order and loads every .env found: 1. An explicit OPENBOX_ENV_FILE path, if set (read before the extra roots). 2. The data directory (the extra root passed to bootstrap_env ). 3. The parent of the data directory. 4. Your home directory ( ~/.env ). 5. ~/.config/openbox-game-launcher/.env . 6. On Windows only, %APPDATA%\openbox-game-launcher and %LOCALAPPDATA%\openbox-game-launcher . The current working directory and the application directory are not searched. Each .env file must be an owner-only regular file (no group or other permission bits; 0o600 is the usual value), must not be a symlink, and must be under 1 MiB; anything else is skipped silently. Windows has no POSIX mode bits, so there the check rejects reparse points instead and otherwise relies on the per-user profile ACL — keep .env inside your own profile directory. Values already in the environment are never overridden by .env . The template lives at .env.example in the repository. Put real secrets in ~/.env or ~/.config/openbox-game-launcher/.env only, never in a tracked file. Only the allowlisted keys are read, so a key in the file that is not in ENV_KEYS is ignored — a value placed in .

title: Data and recovery
description: Understand schema version 7 state files and recovery behavior.
body: The library is one schema-versioned JSON file with a last-known-good sidecar, cross-process locking, and atomic owner-only writes. This page documents the exact layout, the migration path, stable IDs, caps, and recovery. File layout Inside the data directory (default ~/.local/share/openbox-game-launcher , or OPENBOX_DATA_DIR ): Path Purpose --- --- library.json The primary state: format ( openbox-library ), schema_version (7), games , profiles , history , settings , playlists , queue , notifications , ui_state , trash , party_decks , emulator_settings , achievement_overrides , deals , time_capsules , itinerary library.json.bak Last-known-good copy, rewritten before every commit library.json.snapshots/ Rolling snapshots of the last 5 committed states, kept as timestamped JSON copies for point-in-time recovery .library.json.lock Cross-process flock lock coordinating concurrent writers sessions.json Active sessions mirrored out of the library (format 1) for crash recovery; reconciled at startup and removed when no sessions remain library.v6.backup.json Pre-migration copy of the v6 library, written by openbox --migrate-library (or by a 2.0/2.1 first start). OpenBox 3.0 does not restore it; use OpenBox 2.1.0. migration-report.json Record of the v6→v7 migration (counts, sessions moved) migration-in-progress.json Crash marker present while a migration runs; a leftover marker lets startup reconstruct the report migration-acknowledged.json Records that the user has seen the migration report rollback-report.json Legacy 2.0 record of a rollback. 3.0 never writes it. media/manifest.json Per-file SHA-256, size, and mtime for downloads and captures, feeding the integrity check server.token , server.port Per-launch credentials for the running Web UI; deleted on exit Catalog synchronization is separate from this local state directory. When enabled, immutable events live under /openbox-library-v3/ in the mounted folder selected in Settings. The v3 transport does not copy launch paths, commands, credentials, statistics, saves, or media. Write path The Rust JsonStateStore ( crates/openbox-store/src/json_store.rs ) commits like this. The Python state_store.py implementation mirrors it for the fallback. 1. Serialize with compact JSON when the pretty-printed payload exceeds 1 MiB ( COMPACT_JSON_THRESHOLD ) or the library exceeds 500 games; pretty-printed below it; always write a trailing newline. 2. Write to a temp file in the same directory, fsync it, chmod 0o600 . 3. Staged atomic backup: write to temporary backup file and os.replace over library.json.bak , chmod 0o600 . 4. os.replace the primary temp over library.json , chmod 0o600 , then fsync the directory. Every read and write happens under the file lock, so two OpenBoxGL processes (Web UI and native UI) can share one library safely. The last writer wins per transaction, not per file. title: How OpenBoxGL works
description: A code-level guide to startup, state, imports, launching, sessions, jobs, plugins, webhooks, and the local API.
body: The shipped 3.0 backend is the Rust openbox-server ; see [System architecture](/reference/architecture/) for the crate map, state store, native hosts, and job model. The sections below describe the Python fallback ( OPENBOX_BACKEND=python , Python 3.11+) and are kept as a code-level reference for that path. Where a section names web_app.py , handlers/ , pkg/ , or plugin_runner.py , read it as fallback-only. This page is for developers and maintainers who want to follow a real OpenBoxGL operation through the code. It starts at process startup, follows a library entry through import and launch, then covers the workers and extension points that sit around that path. The 3.0 Rust path has the same boundaries; the implementation lives in crates/openbox-cli , crates/openbox-http , crates/openbox-store , crates/openbox-runtime , and the domain crates. OpenBoxGL has a local application core with one presentation layer served by two hosts. The web UI is the loopback HTTP server; on Linux the native window is a small C WebKitGTK shim that spawns openbox-server --no-browser (or python3 web_app.py --no-browser when OPENBOX_BACKEND=python ) and renders the identical index.html , and on Windows the WebView2 host native_host_win.c plays the same role (see [Windows](/windows/)). Both hosts use the same data directory and state-store rules for durable library data, and both run the same server process, so there is no second presentation stack to keep in parity. That distinction explains most of the architecture. Durable facts such as games, settings, playlists, queue entries, notifications, and completed history belong in library.json . Temporary facts such as an open dialog, an active browser selection, a running Popen object, or a queued worker live in memory and disappear when their process stops. , , , , , , , , ]} / The architecture in one view The application is easiest to understand as a set of boundaries around one local library: The composition root is web_app.py , which owns the loopback server and the domain logic. Shared launch and data-directory entry points live in openbox.py . Persistence rules are in state_store.py . The single renderer is index.html ; other modules own narrower rules, such as archive safety, import adapters, metadata, saves, integrations, plugins, themes, and jobs. description: Selected archive items, limits, rollback files, and restore rules.
body: Whole-library backups are ZIP archives in backups/ that can include settings, the library, media, plugins, themes, and extension data. This page documents items, limits, rotation, and restore safety. The implementation is parity_backup.py with contract coverage in test_parity_playnite.py and test_parity_api.py . Archive location and naming - Directory: /backups/ . - Name: OpenBoxBackup-%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S-%f.zip (with microsecond timestamp). - Written via a temp file and os.replace , then the directory is fsynced. Selectable items Key Archive member --- --- settings settings.json (serialized snapshot of state["settings"] ) library library.json (the full state object) media media/ (the media directory tree) plugins plugins/ (installed plugin packages, excluding plugins/credentials/ ) themes themes/ (user themes) extension_data extension-data/ Every archive contains manifest.json : When no items are given, the default is ["library", "settings"] (also used by the CLI --backup ). Backups automatically redact sensitive API keys/passwords, and local credentials are automatically preserved and remerged on restore. Unknown or empty item lists raise "Select at least one backup item." Item names are case-folded and deduplicated. Plugin state in backups Two plugin secrets never enter a backup: - The capability credential store, /plugins/credentials/ (one .json per plugin, mode 0600 ), is skipped entirely when plugins is archived. Credentials are local-only by design, like a device keychain. - plugins-state.json is redacted: every setting whose manifest field declares "format": "password" is written as an empty string, so a required setting still validates on restore. On restore those blanks are merged back from your current local values, so a restore does not wipe a stored plugin secret. If the installed package cannot be read, its settings are copied unchanged rather than guessing which values are secret. It is bundled with the application and refreshed from a commit-pinned repository URL when the network is available. description: The base hook payloads, capability hooks, service requests, and response rules.
body: Plugin API v2 is required in 3.0. A .py entry exports one function per declared hook: def library(payload) , def before_launch(payload) , def after_session(payload) , def command(payload) , def library_source(payload) , def events(payload) , and the capability hooks def storefront(payload) , def metadata(payload) , def media(payload) , def stats(payload) , def emulator(payload) , and def discovery(payload) . A native executable entry receives the same JSON Lines request. The runner calls the matching function with the decoded payload and writes the returned dict as JSON. If the module does not export the hook function, the payload passes through unchanged. The Rust 3.0 server invokes command , events , and the six capability hooks. The library , before_launch , after_session , and library_source hooks are currently invoked only by the Python fallback ( OPENBOX_BACKEND=python ). The Rust server emits app_startup and app_shutdown ; the other lifecycle events are Python-fallback-only. Payloads common to every hook - plugin_data is always present: the plugin's bounded data bag (1 MiB, four levels deep). - settings is present only when the manifest declares a settings schema. Base hooks never see password-format values. - credentials is present only for capability hooks: values from the capability credential store, never password-format settings. library Payload: ]} . The games are the full public projection (every field from GET /api/v2/library , including computed flags like path_exists , has_saves , game_id , and the numeric id ). title: Plugin API overview
description: Trust boundary, the local plugin lifecycle, and capability services.
body: Plugins are optional local packages that observe or extend OpenBoxGL. A v2 entry may be a Python file or a native executable. They are untrusted-by-default third-party code: review a package before installing it, and use safe mode to disable lifecycle hooks and webhooks when something misbehaves. Plugin API v1 was removed in 3.0; every manifest must declare "api_version": 2 . Trust boundary - On Linux, each hook runs inside a bubblewrap OS sandbox when bwrap is available: every namespace is unshared (no network access), the host root is mounted read-only, and /home , /tmp , /run , /mnt , and /media are replaced with empty filesystems. The plugin sees only its own package directory (read-only) and the JSON hook payload on stdin — never your data directory or home folder. - If the sandbox cannot be created, the plugin is skipped rather than run unsandboxed, unless you trust the plugin or set OPENBOX_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_PLUGINS=1 . Two paths exist: per-plugin "Trust and run" in the Plugins manager, which binds the grant to the installed package's SHA-256 (any update that changes the package invalidates the grant and re-prompts), or the legacy operator-wide OPENBOX_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_PLUGINS=1 escape hatch for trusted local code. Reserve unsandboxed execution for plugin code you have read and audited: without the sandbox, the plugin runs as a plain child process with your user privileges and can read and modify files in your data directory and under your account, not only library entries. On Windows bwrap does not exist, so the same per-plugin trust prompt is the only gate. - In both modes the plugin environment is scrubbed before launch: PYTHONPATH , PYTHONHOME , LD_PRELOAD , and LD_LIBRARY_PATH are removed, PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 is set, and any variable whose name contains TOKEN , PASSWORD , SECRET , or API_KEY (case-insensitive) — or starts with OPENBOX_ , RETROACHIEVEMENTS_ , EMUMOVIES_ , GITHUB_ , RA_ , IGDB_ , or GAMEYFIN_ — is stripped, so plugins cannot read tokens, secrets, or host state out of the environment. - Install only packages you wrote or audited. The bundled catalog is documentation-oriented; installing from it still runs downloaded code. Lifecycle 1. Install ( /api/v2/plugins/install ): a directory or ZIP package is staged, validated, and moved into plugins/ / . Updates replace the previous version atomically; a failed install or update restores the previous version. 2. Enable/disable ( /api/v2/plugins/toggle ): disabled plugin ids persist in plugins-state.json ; disabled plugins are skipped by every hook. Disabling also deletes the games the plugin imported and stops its cached stats from merging, while keeping its stored settings, trust, grants, data, and credentials. 3. Run : on each hook event, enabled plugins that declare the hook execute in sorted (alphabetical) directory order, each as a separate process. 4. title: Plugin processes and errors reference
description: Protocol limits, per-hook timeouts, safe mode, and rollback.
body: Every plugin invocation runs in a fresh child process with a JSON Lines frame on stdin/stdout. Plugin API v1 and plugin_runner.py were removed in 3.0; every manifest must declare "api_version": 2 or it fails with PLUGIN_API_RETIRED . This page documents the exact limits and failure handling. Protocol (v2) - A .py entry is started through python3 -B plugin_runner_v2.py ; a native executable entry is started directly. The host writes one frame and reads a result , error , or cancelled frame. - A plugin whose module lacks the hook function gets the input payload and echoes it back. - A plugin whose return value is not a dict falls back to the input payload. - Capability hooks get one optional extra round for service_requests : the host runs at most 8 read-only services and re-invokes the same hook once with service_results . A second request list is dropped with a warning. - Host services are versioned, read-only descriptors ( library.query , media.search ) requested through the runner rather than a re-invoked hook. - There is no persistent runner process; each hook call starts a new process. A timeout kills that process. Limits Limit Value Behavior when exceeded --- --- --- Input payload 2 MiB ( MAX_PLUGIN_PAYLOAD ) The plugin is skipped with "Payload is too large for plugin execution." Output 4 MiB (v2 only) Output beyond the cap is ignored: "Plugin output exceeded the payload limit." Execution time, base hooks 5 seconds The process is killed; a warning is logged and the plugin's result is skipped Execution time, storefront 30 seconds Above Execution time, metadata / media / stats 15 seconds Above Execution time, emulator / discovery 10 seconds Above stderr kept last 400 bytes Included in the failure warning Data bag 1 MiB, 4 levels deep A patch that breaks either bound raises and writes nothing Service requests 8 per hook, one round More than 8 raises "service_requests must be a list of at most 8 requests." ; a second round is ignored Storefront paging 20 pages, 2,000 entries Paging stops; a repeated cursor raises "Plugin storefront pagination repeated a cursor." title: Plugins
description: Build trusted local plugins with the documented manifest, hook, and capability contract.
body: Plugins are local packages that extend OpenBoxGL through documented hooks. A v2 entry may be a Python file or a native executable. They run as separate processes with a JSON Lines protocol, so a plugin that crashes or misbehaves cannot take down the library. Quick facts - Plugin API v1 was removed in 3.0. Every manifest must declare "api_version": 2 ; a missing value or 1 fails with PLUGIN_API_RETIRED . - A plugin manifest ( plugin.json ) requires id , name , and version . IDs match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-] $ ; data , credentials , and plugins-state.json are reserved. - The implementation entry defaults to plugin.py ; explicit entries such as main.py are supported. A .py entry runs through plugin_runner_v2.py ; any other executable entry runs directly. - Base hooks are library , before_launch , after_session , command , library_source , and events (the last three added in v1.14.0). A declared base hook outside this set is rejected. - Capability hooks (1.18.0) are storefront , metadata , media , stats , emulator , and discovery . Each is declared through capabilities , and a capability without its hook is a manifest error. There is no standalone services hook; a capability hook may return service_requests instead. - The runner exchanges one JSON Lines frame per invocation, chains base hooks in sorted (alphabetical by directory) order, caps input at 2 MiB and output at 4 MiB, and stops a plugin after its hook timeout (5 seconds for base hooks; 30 s storefront, 15 s metadata/media/stats, 10 s emulator/discovery). Each hook invocation starts a fresh process. - The plugin environment is cleaned before execution: PYTHONPATH , PYTHONHOME , LD_PRELOAD , and LD_LIBRARY_PATH are removed and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 is set. - Capability hooks also receive a bounded data bag, non-secret settings, and capability credentials. Backups exclude the credential store and blank password-format settings. - Plugins are local code. Review them before installation. Safe mode ( OPENBOX_SAFE_MODE=1 ) skips the lifecycle hooks ( library , before_launch , after_session , library_source , events ) and the webhook dispatcher, but not the capability hooks — an explicit storefront, metadata, media, stats, emulator-settings, or discovery call still invokes that plugin's hook. Failed installations roll back to the previous version. title: Save archives
description: ZIP structure, per-file manifests, preview, selective restore, retention, and validation.
body: Per-game save backups are ZIP archives stored in save-backups/ inside the data directory. This page documents the archive format, where backups live, the preview and selective-restore contract, retention, and the restore safety rules. The implementation is crates/openbox-sync/src/saves.rs (Python saves.py is the fallback), with contract coverage in tests/test_saves.py and tests/test_parity_features.py . Location and naming - Root: /save-backups/ . - Each game has a hash directory derived from its identity: game_backup_dir = SHA-256 of " : " , first 16 hex chars. - Archive names: - .zip where the label is manual , on-close , or before-restore , and the timestamp is YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-ffffff . Names sort newest-first, so list_backups returns the newest archive first. - Labels are validated against [A-Za-z0-9._-] ; anything else raises "Save backup label is invalid." - Backup directories are created with mode 0o700 and existing archives are restricted to 0o600 . Backups are written via a temp file and os.replace , then the directory is fsynced. Archive format A save backup is a ZIP with DEFLATE compression: - manifest.json at the root (capped at 1 MiB): file is true when the root is a single file rather than a directory. label , emulator_id , core , and slot record provenance for the backup list; emulator_id defaults to the game's adapter, and core / slot come from its recorded save source. All provenance strings are truncated to 64 characters. - roots/ /... mirrors each configured save path: for a single-file root, roots/ / ; for a directory root, roots/ / . Manifest entry fields Every regular file is described before it is archived: Field Meaning --- --- root Index into roots , so roots/ / is the archive prefix relative Path relative to the root (the file name for a single-file root) archive Exact ZIP member name size File size in bytes mode Permission bits ( stat.S_IMODE ) mtime Modification time as integer epoch seconds sha256 SHA-256 of the file contents Entries let a restore preview tell an unchanged file from one that would be overwritten, instead of guessing from timestamps. Archives written before 1.18.0 have no entries list; they still restore, but their preview cannot prove a file unchanged, so every present file is reported as an overwrite. What gets backed up backup_saves uses the game's save_paths (configured paths, resolved with expanduser().resolve() ), but only roots that currently exist. Prerequisites and errors: - No configured path currently exists: FileNotFoundError "No configured save paths currently exist." — except for the automatic before-restore safety backup, which is skipped instead of aborting the restore. - Any backup source path is a symlink: ValueError "Save backup paths may not be symlinks." - Any file inside a directory root is a symlink: ValueError "Save backup source contains a symlink: " - Files are opened with O_NOFOLLOW , and anything that is not a regular file raises "Save backup source is not a regular file: " .

title: Search syntax
description: The full grammar of the library search box.
body: The library search box supports field-targeted terms, quoted values, and negative terms. Terms are combined with implicit AND; a space-separated list narrows the results. library.json is the source of truth for search filters, not a separate database you must rebuild. Queries read the in-memory state, or the optional SQLite read model when it is enabled (it also self-enables at 5,000+ games), which accelerates search and facets without changing the grammar or results. Every filter you apply stays in place until you clear it or navigate away, so chaining multiple sidebar facets (e.g. genre → platform → installed) compounds filters without extra typing. The Explorer facets panel (sidebar) does the same thing visually by showing counts per value; clicking a facet injects the equivalent field:value term. See [Library overview](/guides/library/) for the full UI walk-through. Field terms Prefix a term with a field name and a colon to target one field: Field Matches --- --- title: Name, sort title, and alternate names platform: (alias plat: ) Platform value (quote multi-word values: platform:"PlayStation 2" ) dev: (alias developer: ) Developer pub: (alias publisher: ) Publisher series: Series genre: Genre region: Region notes: Notes source: (aliases store: , storefront: ) Import source (Steam, Heroic, Lutris, ...) progress: Progress status status: Status play: (alias playmode: ) Play mode rating: Rating favorite: (alias fav: ) favorite:yes / favorite:no installed: installed:yes / installed:no hidden: (alias hide: ) hidden:yes / hidden:no broken: broken:yes / broken:no portable: portable:yes / portable:no controller: Controller support tag: (alias tags: ) Tag (see below) import_batch_id: (alias import_batch: ) Import batch id, matched exactly rather than as a substring all: Every field at once: name, sort title, alternate names, platform, genre, developer, publisher, series, region, notes, source, play mode, status, progress, controller support, and tags Your own ratings (v1.14.0) Every game carries a personal star rating ( user_rating , 0–5, where 0 is unrated) that is separate from the provider's rating . These clauses read your rating, not the metadata one — they are distinct clause kinds, not aliases of rating: : Form Alias Matches --- --- --- myrating:4 my_rating:4 , my-rating:4 Games you rated 4 or higher (a floor, so myrating:4+ is the same) my 4 stars my rating at least 4 The same floor, in words unrated by me not rated by me Games with no rating from you rating:4 and myrating:4 answer different questions and both are supported side by side. unrated on its own is the provider rating; unrated by me is yours. See [Backlog](/guides/library/backlog/) for where you set a personal rating. Negative terms Prefix any term with - to exclude it: - -tag:demo excludes games carrying a demo tag. - -platform:Windows excludes Windows games. - -title:hollow excludes games whose name contains "hollow". Quoted values Quote values that contain spaces or special char

title: Roadmap
description: What is in the current release, what is in progress, and how to shape what comes next.
body: Roadmap OpenBox is maintained by one person in the open, so the roadmap is short and honest: what is in the current release, what is being worked on, and where new ideas come from. There are no dates and no promises beyond that. In the current release The [changelog](/changelog/) is the accurate record. The latest published release is 3.0.0 — The Rust-y Box . The highlights below cover the 1.19 platform work first, then the 1.18.0 library work: - OpenBox on macOS. A signed universal app bundle runs OpenBox natively on macOS 11 or newer, with the Rust openbox-server , a WKWebView window, the tray, native dialogs, and openbox:// deeplinks. See [macOS](/macos/). - Platform parity. One server-computed capability contract hides Linux-only controls on Windows and macOS, the Windows battery reports real values, and the storefront list matches each host. See [API 1.19 changes](/reference/api/one-nineteen/). - A clearer first run. The top bar folds four add actions into one Add games menu. The setup dialog, Set up your library , opens on a six-step quick path with the longer optional steps behind an advanced toggle, and Help & shortcuts ( F1 or ? ) adds a glossary and the real shortcut table. The default palette separates the orange action colour from the teal focus colour, and Play Insights now sits below the grid. title: Steam Deck and handhelds
description: Run OpenBox on Steam Deck, Bazzite, and handheld PCs, in Game Mode or on the desktop.
body: Steam Deck and handhelds OpenBox targets Steam Deck, Bazzite, and other Linux handheld PCs. On the desktop it behaves like any Linux app; in Steam Game Mode it runs as a guest inside Steam's gamescope session so Steam Input, the Quick Access Menu (TDP/FPS), and MangoHud stay with Steam. Install Prefer the signed AppImage on SteamOS, Bazzite, and other immutable images. The AppImage ships the Rust server with no Python runtime, works without installing anything system-wide, and receives the built-in verified updater. For a reproducible install, download the script for the tag you pinned (v3.0.0), inspect it, then run it: Choose the AppImage matching the handheld CPU; set OPENBOX_ARCH=x86_64 or OPENBOX_ARCH=aarch64 only when automatic architecture detection needs an override. See [Installation](/install/) for AppImage, Flatpak, and source options. Run in Steam Game Mode 1. Install the AppImage (preferred on SteamOS, Bazzite, and other immutable images). 2. In Desktop Mode, add a non-Steam game pointing at the AppImage, with launch options or target args including --game-mode . 3. Enable Steam Input for that shortcut if you want controller profiles in Big Box. 4. Return to Game Mode and launch OpenBox. It opens Big Box fullscreen. Do not wrap OpenBox in another gamescope while already in Game Mode. On a normal desktop, behavior is unchanged unless you pass --game-mode . The Flatpak build relies on host tools for the kiosk-browser window tagging, so prefer the AppImage for Game Mode. How Game Mode works OpenBox detects the gamescope guest via environment ( GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY , STEAM_GAMESCOPE_RESTRICTED , or a gamescope desktop name) and opens Big Box fullscreen in the native window. In the web fallback ( --web , or when the native host is missing), the UI opens in a kiosk browser (Chromium, Chrome, Brave, or Edge, native or Flatpak), and OpenBox marks that window with a dedicated STEAM_GAME id ( 413091001 ) so it is visible under gamescope. Steam titles launched from OpenBox still go through Steam ( steam -applaunch / steam:// ), so Steam Input and overlays keep working. Non-Steam games get a stable synthetic STEAM_GAME id derived from their identity, in the range 700,000,000 to 899,999,999. The tagging is a window property only; it does not change how the game runs. OpenBox does not provide live in-game TDP controls — use Steam's QAM or your image's handheld tools for changes during a session. It can apply an optional per-launch TDP cap through ryzenadj , with an optional restore value when the session ends; see [Handheld performance profiles]( handheld-performance-profiles) below. Developers can approximate Deck/Bazzite Game Mode on a desktop with ./scripts/emulate_deck_gamemode.sh (requires gamescope; runs a nested session with SteamDeck=1 advertising). Handheld performance profiles Per-launch-profile TDP limits apply via ryzenadj at launch, with an optional restore limit when the session ends. The Apply handheld performance limits setting

title: Themes
description: Choose stock themes or import a local CSS theme.
body: Themes are plain CSS files with instant apply: changing the active theme re-applies instantly without restarting. Six stock themes ship with OpenBoxGL and are installed into the user themes folder automatically at startup: - Midnight Circuit : dark blue-black palette with cyan accents. - Phosphor Terminal : dark green terminal palette. - Harbor Light : light paper-toned palette with blue and coral accents. - Cinema Marquee : dark cinema palette with gold accents. - Nordic Mist : dark slate palette with muted teal accents. - High Contrast : maximum-contrast palette added in v1.15.0 — body text at 21:1 against pure black, with AAA foregrounds. Apply a theme Open Tools → Themes . Choose a scope: All platforms or one specific platform, then pick the theme from Active theme (Default resets). Apply saves the choice; per-platform themes override the global one when viewing that platform. The theme is served from the user themes folder ( /themes ) with revalidation headers, so editing a CSS file on disk shows up after reload. The dialog is a swatch gallery rather than a bare list: each card, including Default, shows five color chips sampled from --bg , --surface-card , --brand , --text , and --muted , so the palette is visible before you apply it. A custom theme should define all five (see [token requirements](/guides/themes/custom-themes/ design-system-tokens)). Import your own CSS Import CSS theme takes an absolute path to a .css file and copies it into the themes folder. Open themes folder opens the folder (after ensuring stock themes are present). Imported themes are plain CSS: they override the base stylesheet, so they can restyle the library, detail pane, dialogs, and Big Box. Stock themes carry a / OpenBox Stock Theme: marker. On startup, missing stock themes are re-installed, but user edits to a stock file are preserved, and user-imported files without the marker are never touched. Theme music and sounds (v1.18.0) A theme may ship background music and move/select/back sounds through a sidecar JSON file next to its CSS. Play theme music and navigation sounds in Big Box ( bigbox_sounds_enabled , default on) enables them; music starts when Big Box opens and stops when it closes. A missing or malformed sidecar is silent. See [Theme music and sounds](/guides/themes/custom-themes/ theme-music-and-sounds-v1180) for the file format and route details. Authoring guidance The public design tokens live in the [Design system](/project/design-system/) page. In short: the default look is dark, warm surfaces, off-white text, a brand-orange action ramp ( --brand and --active FF7A1A , --action F58A2E , --action-ink 1A120A ) and a teal focus signal ( --focus 5FD3C4 ). Themes may change palette and surface treatment while preserving the interaction structure; do not rely on undocumented theme-specific font-family claims. Keep readable contrast on both light and dark surfaces, visible focus states (the base stylesheet outlines focused controls), and legible controls;

title: Updating
description: Update OpenBoxGL 3.0, migrate a library from 2.x or 1.x, and understand the package boundaries.
body: OpenBoxGL 3.0 ships the Rust openbox-server with no bundled Python. The in-app update check works on every platform, but the verified install step is implemented for the AppImage only. Windows and macOS install a new release by running the new release's installer. Flatpak, source, and system installs follow their own package or source workflow. Upgrading to 3.0 3.0 keeps library schema 7, backup format 2, sync format 3, and /api/v2 . A 2.0 or 2.1 library opens without migration. The breaks run the other way: 3.0 will not boot a schema 6 file, will not run a v1 plugin, will not roll a library back, and will not start on Python 3.10. Before you upgrade - If the library is still schema 6 (a 1.19 library that 2.1 has not opened yet): quit OpenBox, then either run openbox --migrate-library on 3.0 or open the library once on 2.1 before you install 3.0. Startup does not upgrade it. The command keeps library.v6.backup.json . - If the library is schema 1 through 5: open it on OpenBox 2.1 before you install 3.0. 3.0 migrates schema 6 only and does not rewrite an older file. - If a plugin omits api_version or still says 1 : set "api_version": 2 and follow the [plugin reference](/reference/plugins/). 3.0 does not run the v1 runner; the manifest fails with PLUGIN_API_RETIRED . - If you run from source on Python 3.10: install Python 3.11 or newer before you start the fallback. The Rust server itself needs no Python. - If you still need openbox --rollback-library : that command is gone. OpenBox 2.1.0 is the last build that restores library.v6.backup.json . 3.0 does not delete a backup that is already on disk. Upgrade 1. Quit OpenBox. 2. If the library is older than schema 7, migrate it as described above. A schema 7 library needs no migration. 3. Install 3.0 over 2.1, or over an older build after the library is schema 7. 4. Start OpenBox. GET /api/v2/version reports version 3.0.0, api_version 2, state_schema 7, plugin_api_version 2, backup_format 2, sync_format 3, and runtime: "rust" . What did not change - Library schema 7, the required envelope, and backup format 2 (format 1 is still read). - Sync format 3. - The public API at /api/v2 and the host channel at /api/host . - The SQLite read model: it is still a projection. Deleting sqlite_readmodel.db loses nothing. - The AppImage glibc floor ( GLIBC_2.35 on Ubuntu 22.04). What you cannot do in 3.0 - Roll the library back to the v6 copy. Use OpenBox 2.1.0 if you still have library.v6.backup.json and need that restore. - Start the Python fallback on Python 3.10. - Load a plugin whose manifest is missing api_version or sets it to 1. Upgrading from 2.0 or 2.1 2.1 installs over 2.0 and makes the 2.0 contracts permanent: the public API is /api/v2 only, the /api/v1 bridge and unversioned /api/ aliases are gone, backups write format 2 only, and the media checksum toggle takes effect. 3.0 installs over 2.1 with no library migration. If you are coming from 2.0, note that 2.0's /api/v1 bridge and 1.19-compatible backup ex

title: Windows
description: Install and run OpenBoxGL on Windows with the signed portable installer, the PowerShell launchers, and the WebView2 native window.
body: OpenBoxGL runs natively on Windows as of 1.13.0. There is no MSI, no installer wizard, no account, and no license key: the portable installer verifies a signed release, lays the runtime down under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenBox , and adds the launchers to your user PATH . The Windows zip ships the same Rust openbox-server that runs on Linux and macOS, plus the WebView2 host native_host.exe . The library format, the web UI, the HTTP API, the plugins, and the emulator definitions are identical across platforms, so a library directory moves between Linux, Windows, and macOS unchanged. Install from a signed release Download the release archive from the tag you want, extract it, and run the bundled installer at OpenBox\scripts\install.ps1 . The installer pins the release public key, verifies its SHA-256 against a committed anchor, and verifies the archive's .sha256 sidecar and Ed25519 signature before extracting anything. Omit -Tag to install the latest release instead of the pinned one above; the current release is 3.0.0 . Pass -Run to start OpenBox when the install finishes: Run the script from the extracted OpenBox\scripts\ folder. It resolves the release verifier ( updates.py ) one directory above itself, and the verifier is the trust anchor for the Ed25519 check, so it is never downloaded on its own — a fetched verifier could be replaced by whoever served it. The release also publishes install.ps1 as a standalone asset, but it is the same installer that ships inside the archive, so a standalone copy only works from the extracted release, where updates.py is one directory above it. The installer always fetches the archive for your architecture ( OpenBox-x86_64-windows.zip or OpenBox-arm64-windows.zip ), its .sha256 , and its .sig from the release tag into a fresh temp directory — placing those files next to the script yourself has no effect.
